old_description:
Upgrade catalog-ui to Angular 8

Upgrade the Angular CLI workspace to Angular 8.2.14, CLI 8.3.29 and TypeScript 3.5.3. Retain View Engine, development JIT, production AOT, hashbang routing and gzip packaging.

Migrate legacy HTTP and RxJS APIs, preserve silent offline plugin probes, update query timing and align NGXS, UI dependencies and Jest.

Stack above WIP CR 148981 (SDC-5204). The current SDC release must finish before that parent merges. This consumer also requires the compatible onap-ui-angular 6.0.0 release tracked by SDC-5209; local verification currently uses its candidate tarball, not a published stable artifact.

Local verification passed 1505 tests, 18 snapshots, AOT/gzip and nine production browser smoke tests. The full browser run had 96 passes, one skip and an onboarding accessibility failure reproduced on the unchanged FE. Maven packaging, registry-artifact validation and voting CI remain pending.

Issue-ID: SDC-5210

Move the ngSwitch inside the datatable cell templates: ngx-datatable
15 resolves them with static queries, which cannot see a template
under a structural directive, so the Import VSP and capability
properties tables fell back to raw values.

new_description:
[SDC] 13.5.0

- update sdc images (1.19.0 -> 1.20-20261104T070822Z)
- poll the distribution status topic every 5s instead of every 60s
- start sdc-fe with the image's entrypoint and pass its Jetty settings
as system properties

SDC-BE polls SDC-DISTR-STATUS-TOPIC once per pollingIntervalSec, and each
poll returns the records fetched by the previous one. A consumer's
status therefore reached the distribution status API 64-115s after it
was sent, which made every distributing test wait ~2 minutes even when
all consumers finished within ~40s.

sdc-frontend is now an executable jar with embedded Jetty instead of a
Jetty distribution with two WARs, so the start.jar command the chart
ran no longer exists. The chart drops that command; the image's
startup.sh adds the same system properties and the OpenTelemetry agent
and runs the jar. The start.d http.ini, https.ini and ssl.ini mounts and
rewrite-root-to-sdc1.xml go with their configmaps: the server reads
the same jetty.* properties, which JAVA_OPTIONS now carries
(fe_conf.http_port, fe_conf.https_port and the optional keystore and
truststore values), and redirects / to /sdc1 itself.

The images are built from sdc master d9ac3f4b9. This includes the
catalog-be servlet and filter registration in Java, the jersey-spring5
and Jersey 2.35 migration, the Java Spring configuration, the
configuration bootstrap changes, the Spring Boot 2.7 BOM import and
the executable sdc-frontend jar.

Snapshot images published by sdc-maven-docker-stage-master build 1564.

the current AAI DTOs and tested SO classes. The checkout parent remains

All 63 selected positive NSI helper tests pass three clean runs without

pass and the TN context case reports MissingPropertyException. Normal
execution passes nine and explicitly skips that guard. The 494 scenario

restoration passes. Production sources remain unchanged.

Exercise the shipped NSI parent and real child allocations from seeded

checking typed results, per-domain identities and exact external actions.
Verify deployed parent and child resources against packaged BPMN bytes.

Routing tests retain activity history and read returned process variables.
Separate FULL-history tests preserve persistence checks: BH passes while

The strict profile exposes those errors; normal execution explicitly
skips those three guards. No database column or production code changed.

The four positive cases pass three clean runs on each backend without
reruns or native database leaks. Both strict backend runs execute seven
cases: four pass and three fail with the intended history error. Normal
H2 execution passes four and skips the three named guards. The 501
scenario mappings pass. An inverted FH/MH gateway choice is caught by the
missing FH identity; restoring the production BPMN passes the same test.

Protect the three shared SDNC request builders with namespace-aware
payload contracts for feature requests, VNF activation, VPN assignment,
VNI activation/deletion, escaped values and ordered repeated inputs.
Assert independent header/body identities and generated request IDs
without fixing harmless XML formatting or independent field order.

511 scenario mappings pass. Private callback and action faults are caught
and restoration passes. These three helpers have no literal production
caller; their module-only scenarios do not claim process-route coverage.
Production code remains unchanged.

Protect VF-module deletion response parsing and inventory cleanup
payloads with ten further helper contracts. Check typed completion,
namespaced outputs, ordered policy identities, management addresses,
business errors, escaped identities and conditional DELETE sentinels.

All 14 new and original Groovy deletion tests pass three clean strict
runs and a normal run without skips or retries. The 521 scenario mappings
pass. Private error-code and management-address faults are caught and
restoration passes. This batch characterizes callable helpers; it does
not claim complete lifecycle or process-route protection.

Execute the shipped VF-module deletion process from the post-adapter
boundary for absent, explicit null, empty, wrong-operation and malformed
responses. Assert the persisted typed business error, termination before
inventory/controller cleanup and absence of child process execution.
Compare deployed BPMN bytes with its production resource.

All five H2 process cases pass three clean strict runs and a normal run
without skips or retries. A private error-code fault fails the named
process contract; restoration passes. The 526 scenario mappings pass.
These cases protect the local failure routes; they do not establish
caller-boundary handling or the complete deletion lifecycle.

Protect VF-module deletion request construction with seven further
contracts for escaped identities, VNF callback correlation, missing
callback configuration, SDNC action/namespace fields, resource retention,
inventory-name fallback and opaque generated request IDs.

All 21 selected request, response and original Groovy tests pass three
clean strict runs and a normal run without skips or retries. The 533
scenario mappings pass. Private skip-AAI and resource-retention faults
are caught and restoration passes. Production sources remain unchanged.

Protect policy cleanup for absent/empty lists, typed counts and status,
escaped FQDN queries, returned inventory identities, externally visible
deletion order and preservation of the original failure when no cleanup
is requested. Mock only the external inventory client boundary.

Strict execution runs all nine cases: seven pass and two expose the same
error-propagation defect. The helper catches its own deletion error 2500
and continues later policy actions. Normal execution explicitly skips
these first/last-deletion guards. Production code remains unchanged.

All 28 selected positive new and original deletion tests pass three clean
runs with no reruns; normal execution passes 28 and skips two guards.
The 542 scenario mappings pass. Runtime provider checks match the tested
sources. Disposable FQDN-query and returned-identity faults are caught
and restoration passes. These results do not declare a protected slice.

Execute the real parent and shared inventory-deletion child at the
final VF-module inventory stage. Cover addon/base/last-module and VID
retention routes, absent resources, query failure and failure at both
deletion stages. Check exact inventory-client actions, query depth,
typed call mappings and business errors returned to the parent.

Reopen the engine before checking persisted completed history. A normal
parent end does not prove business success: error cases assert the typed
WorkflowException out mapping. Do not infer outer-caller error handling,
wait-state resumption or full deletion lifecycle protection.

All 14 selected H2 process cases pass three clean strict runs and a normal
run without skips or reruns. The nine new cases also pass on local
MariaDB with owned database cleanup. All 12 original shared Groovy
inventory-deletion tests pass. The overnight machine pause is excluded
from performance interpretation; no suite-duration estimate is made.

The 551 scenario mappings and 21 runtime-provider comparisons pass.
Deployed parent/child resources match their actual packaged bytes and
current production sources. A private child-input mapping fault removes
the expected inventory actions; its named contract fails and restoration
passes. Production sources remain unchanged.

Protect VF-module update adapter and inventory payload construction
with thirteen further contracts. Check independent request/callback IDs,
escaped identities, real parameter merging, false/zero values, backout,
optional metadata presence, updated status and malformed-input errors.
Distinguish an absent module, an empty stack and a null stack property;
the last currently produces literal null text on the wire.

Strict execution runs all thirteen cases: eleven pass and two expose
unescaped optional values in the generic-VNF and VF-module inventory
builders. Both report the current 1002 error; no production fix is made.
Normal execution explicitly skips those guards with their reason.

All eighteen selected positive new and original Groovy update tests pass
three clean runs without reruns. Normal execution passes eighteen and
skips the two guards. The 564 scenario mappings pass. Fourteen provider
comparisons match production at the fetched base and the existing CR's
configurable-port test fixture. Private backout and inventory-status
faults are caught and restoration passes. No protected slice is declared.

Exercise the shipped shared generic-VNF and VF-module inventory update
processes in Camunda with nineteen further contracts. Mock only the
external inventory client. Check exact paths, query depth where requested,
typed patches, absent/empty/DELETE behavior, model invariants and the
legacy module model fallback. Check query and update error routes and
distinguish a disappeared module from an update transport failure.

Reopen the engine before asserting completed history and typed business
errors. These synchronous processes do not establish wait-state resume
compatibility or protection of their complete parent workflows.

Strict execution passes seventeen cases and exposes two existing model
mismatch logging errors, one in each helper. The logger rejects an
Exception-only error call before the intended workflow error is recorded.
Normal execution skips those two guards explicitly; no production repair
is included. Retain the original ignored generic-VNF Groovy fixture.

The seventeen positive cases pass three clean H2 runs and local MariaDB
without reruns. Normal execution passes seventeen and skips two guards.
All six original VF-module Groovy update tests and all 593 scenario
mappings pass. Runtime sources and deployed resources match the fetched
production base. Private identity, query-error-code and suppressed-update
faults fail named assertions and restoration passes. No slice is declared
protected and no whole-reactor baseline is claimed.

Add ten fast request contracts using the public DelegateExecution API
with stateful variables. Assert namespaced escaped identities, string
false/zero optional values, clearing of stale query/update state and exact
2000 errors for absent or empty required VNF/module IDs. All sixteen new
and original VF-module Groovy cases pass three clean focused runs and a
normal run without skips or reruns. A private required-field error-code
fault is detected and restoration passes. Production sources remain unchanged.

Protect shared AAI exception mapping with twelve further contracts.
Assert structured fault substitution and precedence over transport
fallbacks, supplied generic/REST fault codes, malformed-response fallback,
and namespace-aware fallout requests retaining child error identity,
origin and work step. Compare parsed XML fields rather than formatting.

Strict execution passes ten cases and exposes two failures from treating
business fault values as regex replacements: dollar signs trigger an
error and backslashes disappear. These are two cases of one failure mode.
Normal execution explicitly skips both guards; no production fix is made.

All 28 selected positive new, existing Java and original Groovy exception
tests pass three clean runs without skips or reruns. Normal execution
passes 28 and skips three guards, including the existing SO-4443 guard.
All 615 scenario mappings and twelve runtime-provider comparisons pass.
Private structured-fault priority and missing fallout-request faults fail
named assertions and restoration passes. No protected slice is declared.

Add ten callback and rollback configuration contracts using the real
shared service-task processor and URN reader. Cover independent internal
and external endpoints, UTF-8 path-segment escaping, trailing slashes,
missing/empty endpoint errors and exact Boolean rollback values. Keep
Boolean overrides distinct from string/numeric values that use the
configured default, and preserve unrelated prefixed state.

All nineteen selected new and original Groovy service-task tests pass
three clean runs and a normal run without skips or reruns. Twelve
provider comparisons match the tested sources, including the actual URN
reader. Private encoding and inverted rollback faults fail named tests
and restoration passes. Production sources remain unchanged.

Exercise service-instance rollback inventory routes with ten further
Camunda contracts. Execute the real Java deletion delegate and resolve
its node URI through a mocked external inventory lookup before checking
the canonical deletion target, eligibility and error routes.

Start the production caller at its rollback entry and execute its actual
child call mappings. Assert restoration of the parent's saved original
error after cleanup fails, fresh child scope despite a parent skip flag,
and persisted completion after reopening the engine. Disabled compensation
retains its Boolean false outcome for uncompensated created resources.

Strict execution passes nine cases and exposes an unset failed-cleanup
outcome where the rollback contract requires Boolean false. Normal
execution explicitly skips that guard. No production repair is included.

The nine positive cases pass three clean H2 runs without skips or reruns.
Normal execution passes nine and skips one guard. A child success and a
parent/child cleanup-failure scenario pass on owned local MariaDB with
native cleanup. All ten original helper tests and 625 mappings pass.

Thirty-eight runtime class/resource comparisons match the tested sources.
Private gateway suppression and success-outcome faults fail named tests;
restoration passes. Scope covers rollback entry/call mappings and inventory
routes; creation-stage faults, controller compensation and wait-state
resumption need separate scenarios. No protected slice is declared.

Exercise service-instance controller compensation through the shipped
SDNCAdapterV1 SOAP process. Check deactivate/delete order, exact wire
identities, authorization and callback URL, callback waits after engine
reopen, duplicate rejection and inventory cleanup after controller success.
Use local HTTP and inventory boundaries with the actual URN reader.

Strict execution passes five cases and exposes false rollback success
after a failed delete callback, followed by inventory deletion. The shipped
delete post-processing script has no scriptFormat. Normal execution skips
that guard explicitly. No production BPMN or helper repair is included.

The five positive controller cases pass three clean H2 runs without skips
or reruns. Normal execution passes five and skips one guard. Two successful
controller scenarios pass on owned local MariaDB. All five original SDNC
Groovy helper tests and all 631 scenario mappings pass.

Strengthen the existing deployment smoke using original resource names,
exact per-resource process keys and persisted byte equality. All 242
production resources pass three clean focused runs. Normal execution keeps
the three existing profile-only inventory checks explicitly skipped.

Runtime class and all packaged-resource comparisons match the fetched
production base. Disposable gateway and outbound-action faults are caught
and restoration passes. Record the missing-language diagnostic separately
from baseline and sensitivity evidence. No protected slice is declared.

Protect VNF request preprocessing with ten further contracts using a
stateful public DelegateExecution mock and the actual OOF and URN helpers.
Mock only the external catalog client. Check named typed identities,
Unicode/escaped request information, model/controller defaults, UUIDs,
homing region publication and preservation of other rollback families.

Require both the numeric BPMN error and WorkflowException code 2000 for
absent or blank callbacks, before catalog access. Keep the two cloud-region
consumers consistent when homing succeeds; retain the caller region when
homing is missing or unavailable. Do not freeze incidental write order.

All eleven new and original Groovy cases pass three clean focused runs
and normal execution without skips or reruns. All 641 scenario mappings
and thirty runtime-provider comparisons pass. Private callback-code and
rollback-region faults fail named assertions; restoration passes.
Production sources remain unchanged. These callable-helper cases do not
claim complete VNF lifecycle, process-route or protected-slice coverage.

Execute the shipped default VNF creation process from initialization
through service lookup, inventory creation, relationship and completion.
Mock only external inventory/catalog clients. Assert typed payloads,
Unicode, absent model IDs, string zero/false, exact mutation ordering,
business errors and absence of unexpected client actions.

Cover service absence, lookup failure, rejected creation and failure after
creation. The latter exposes missing rollback identity and eligibility for
the externally created VNF. Strict verification runs that guard; normal
execution skips it explicitly. No production bookkeeping repair is made.

The six positive scenarios pass three clean H2 runs without skips or
reruns. Normal execution passes six and skips one guard. A success and a
post-creation relationship failure also pass on owned local MariaDB.
All 648 scenario mappings and 49 runtime-provider/resource comparisons pass.

Disposable payload-omission and suppressed-relationship faults fail the
named success contract and restoration passes. Reopening completed history
checks typed persistence; this does not establish wait-state resumption,
the outer compensation caller or the SDNC-enabled journey. The production
default intentionally disables SDNC interaction. No slice is declared protected.

Protect service-instance resolution with seven further contracts using
the actual lazy AAI URI resolver and a stateful public execution mock.
Assert exact node identity and pathed format, typed customer/subscription
keys and resource link, alias isolation and read-only inventory operations.

Preserve 2500 when availability is false and 7000 for transport or later
metadata-resolution failures, including malformed and empty node results.
Check both numeric BPMN and WorkflowException codes without publishing
fresh service context on those failures.

All eighteen selected lookup, request and original Groovy cases pass three
clean focused runs and normal execution without skips or reruns. The 655
scenario mappings and 32 provider comparisons pass. Private wrong-alias
and error-code faults fail named assertions and restoration passes.
Production sources remain unchanged. This batch adds callable lookup
contracts and does not claim additional process-route protection.

Standalone engine scenarios currently register the connector plugin and
omit SO application parse plugins. Application call-activity exception
propagation and business-key handling require separate app-module tests
before deployment-level route protection can be claimed.

Move index document serialization to the search adapter

Replace IndexDocument.getAsJson with structured document objects. Build
suggestion payloads with maps and lists, and carry documents through the
synchronizers and asynchronous PUT task to SearchServiceAdapter. Keep the
legacy REST client's required string encoding at that transport boundary.
Merge existing documents without intermediate JSON strings.

Issue-ID: AAI-4315
new_description:
Move index document serialization to the search adapter

Replace IndexDocument.getAsJson with typed search documents. A new
SearchDocument interface marks what the search service indexes:
SearchableEntity and IndexableCrossEntityReference, which serialize
themselves, AggregationDocument and SuggestionDocument (with
SuggestionPayload and SuggestionFilter) for the aggregation and
suggestion entities, and MergableEntity for documents merged into an
existing one. The synchronizers, PerformSearchServicePut and
SearchServiceAdapter.putDocument and buildBulkImportOperationRequest
accept only SearchDocument, and the adapter serializes it with Jackson
at the legacy string-based RestClient. Merges use ObjectMapper.updateValue
instead of round trips through JSON strings.

Decode aggregation buckets with Jackson in the search adapter, requiring
objects, arrays and textual keys rather than silently accepting bad data.

The synchronizer tests now stub putDocument. The search adapter tests
cover nested aggregations and malformed responses, and the entity tests
check the document structure, escaped values and the merge.

strings wrapped in OperationResult. Enable Jackson REST binding only on
the two migrated endpoints and preserve the existing response fields,
empty details object, omitted null personalization values and error body.

Add HTTP contract coverage for disabled/enabled subscriptions, escaped

Issue-ID: AAI-4315
new_description:
Let Camel serialize configuration responses

Return subscription and personalization response objects from the bean
methods instead of JSON strings wrapped in OperationResult, and enable
Jackson REST binding only on the two migrated endpoints. Subscription
details become a typed SubscriptionDetails object that omits null values.

Failures are handled by an onException clause in each router, which
logs the error and answers HTTP 500 with an empty body. Previously both
endpoints answered 200 with "{}": the personalization code set a 500
result code that never reached the response. sparky-fe already reports
a warning for these statuses, and the error is only reachable with a
null configuration value.

Add HTTP contract coverage for disabled/enabled subscriptions, escaped
values, null fields and the subscription error response.

## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

old_description:
CI: Add SonarCloud branch analysis on security-workflows

Branch analysis for this project runs only on Jenkins, as the job

ccsdk-sli-sonar

built from the global-jjb gerrit-maven-sonar template. Add a GitHub
Actions lane that calls the security-workflows reusable, so the
analysis travels with the shared workflow rather than with a
per-project Jenkins job definition.

The lane reports to the same SonarCloud project the Jenkins job uses:

onap_ccsdk-sli

so the analysis history is continuous rather than forked onto a
parallel project.

Triggers mirror the Jenkins job rather than the verify lanes added
elsewhere in this migration. gerrit-maven-sonar runs weekly on master
and on demand; it is not a per-patchset gate. This lane therefore runs
on a weekly schedule and on manual dispatch, and adds no patchset
trigger.

The filename deliberately omits 'gerrit'. That substring is what opts
a workflow into gerrit_to_platform dispatch, and this lane must not run
against a patchset: it analyses the long-lived branch, so dispatching
it per change would re-scan master on every patchset. Lanes that
analyse a long-lived branch are named without the prefix for that
reason; lanes that are meant to be dispatched per change keep it.

The lane does not vote. The Jenkins job sets skip-vote on every
outcome, so Sonar has never gated a change here, and this does not
change that. For the same reason the quality gate is neither awaited
nor enforced, matching sonarcloud-qualitygate-wait being false.

Unlike a per-patchset lane, this one writes the project's own branch
analysis -- the headline dashboard numbers. Two choices follow from
that. sonar_branch_name is left unset because maven-sonar.sh only sets
sonar.branch.name when scan-dev-branch is true, which this template
leaves false. analysis_mode is left unset so the reusable derives
sonar-maven-plugin from build_type: the Scanner CLI walks
target/generated-sources and reports findings against generated code,
which has taken a project from 0 bugs to over a thousand while still
reporting success.

The pre-scan build is 'clean install', matching the Jenkins job, so the
Java analyser sees bytecode and the JaCoCo report; a source-only scan
reports no coverage. java_version is left unset so the reusable detects
the project's JDK rather than pinning a value that can drift out of
step with the POMs.

The Jenkins job is left in place and still runs. Rollback is turning
this workflow off. Retire the Jenkins job only once a scheduled run
here is shown to agree with it.

new_description:
[MULTICLOUD] 13.5.0 release

- [k8s] update image (0.13.0 -> 0.14.0-SNAPSHOT-20261030T121640Z,
k8s 9f8422c, build multicloud-k8s-master-docker-golang-shell-daily/1914)
- [k8s] update artifactbroker image (1.9.4 ->
1.10-STAGING-20261030T121536Z, framework 488d35b, build
multicloud-framework-maven-docker-stage-master/1397)
- [k8s] configure the Spring Boot artifactbroker with
config/application.yaml instead of the policy-distribution
config.json, and start it with the image's entrypoint
- [k8s] probe the artifactbroker on /actuator/health/liveness and
/actuator/health/readiness instead of a TCP socket
- [k8s] give the artifactbroker a startupProbe (5 s x 30). Spring Boot
takes ~28 s to start under the 600m CPU limit, which left the 10 s /
30 s liveness probe only about 70 s before it restarted the container
- [k8s] drop the artifactbroker's /data emptyDir and the
volumes.artifactDataSizeLimit value; charts are kept in memory
- [k8s] move the artifactbroker's SDC consumer credentials out of the
ConfigMap into an sdc-creds basicAuth secret (overridable with
artifactbroker.sdc.credsExternalSecret) and pass them as
ARTIFACTBROKER_SDC_USER / ARTIFACTBROKER_SDC_PASSWORD
- [k8s] pass TRACING_ENABLED, TRACING_SAMPLING_PROBABILITY,
COLLECTOR_HOST and COLLECTOR_PORT (OTLP gRPC) to the artifactbroker,
and default global.tracing.sampling.probability to 1.0
- [k8s] add a ServiceMonitor for the artifactbroker's
/actuator/prometheus on container port 9014 (rendered when
global.metrics.enabled). It selects the port with targetPort, so the
NodePort service does not have to publish 9014
- [k8s] add an AuthorizationPolicy. Allowed are the callers OOM
configures with a multicloud-k8s:9015 URL: so-cnf-adapter and
so-openstack-adapter (multicloud.endpoint), cds-blueprints-processor
(blueprintprocessor.k8s.plugin.url) and robot
(GLOBAL_MC_K8S_SERVER_PORT), plus istio-ingress for the optional
ingress. The multicloud broker is not listed: it reaches plugins
through MSB, which OOM no longer deploys
- [k8s] give resources.unlimited real requests and limits, as the ONAP
umbrella selects it via global.flavor and the pod was BestEffort
- [k8s] size the artifactbroker with its own artifactbroker.resources
instead of the k8s plugin's map
- [k8s] drop initialDelaySeconds from the artifactbroker's liveness and
readiness probes, which wait for the startupProbe anyway
- bump multicloud-k8s chart 13.4.0 -> 13.5.0 and multicloud
chart 15.3.0 -> 15.4.0

old_description:
Patch the AAA and pax-web versions Titanium ships

installation/sdnc copies two patched jars from Highstreet into the
Karaf system repository: aaa-authn-api and pax-web-jetty. Their versions
were still pinned to 0.20.8 and 8.0.27, but the ODL Titanium
distribution (onap-karaf 0.22.1) ships aaa-authn-api 0.21.2 and
pax-web-jetty 8.0.33. The jars were therefore copied into version
directories that no feature references, and neither patch was active.

This change moves both patches to the versions Titanium ships. Both are
published on Maven Central under com.highstreet-technologies, and the
jars in the image match Maven Central's sha1. That is checked by
image-contract.sh, which comes with the next change. It also checks that
each artifact has only the one version directory, so a patch cannot
silently end up in an unused version directory again.

Runtime check: in the image built by the next change, Karaf reports no
failed bundle with these jars in place (diag: ACTIVE=466, FAILURE=0;
the single WAITING bundle is the unrelated ansible-adaptor). On the
current base image Karaf does not get that far (see the next change), so
CSIT cannot test this change on its own.

old_description:
Build the listener images on eclipse-temurin

The ueb-listener and dmaap-listener images only needed three things from
ccsdk-alpine-j21-image: Java, bash and the JAVA_OPTS default. With
those they also shipped 84 other packages (mariadb, python3, nodejs,
git, graphviz, sudo, rsync, ...), and they got a JDK or Alpine fix only
after a ccsdk/distribution release. They now start from eclipse-temurin
(java.base.image in the root pom) and add only bash. After this change
ansible-server is the only image built by sdnc/oam that still depends
on a ccsdk/distribution image, and the ccsdk.docker.alpine.* properties
are removed.

As for sdnc-image, the image runs apk upgrade at build time, so it
picks up current Alpine fixes even when the pinned temurin tag is no
longer rebuilt. The previously pinned eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7 tag
still had libexpat 2.7.5, while Alpine ships 2.9.0. Without the upgrade
those listener images had more OS-package CVEs than the same images
built from master on the old base.

CVEs (Trivy, one run with the same DB, 2026-10-23):

critical high medium low
sdnc-ueb-listener-image 3.2.4 14 179 240 78
this change 0 14 27 2
sdnc-dmaap-listener-image 3.2.4 19 192 244 84
this change 5 29 31 8

None of the remaining findings is in an OS package; they are all in the
listeners' own jars.

3.2.4 -> this change: ueb-listener 1.02 GB -> 538 MB, dmaap-listener
1.06 GB -> 580 MB, 157 -> 75 apk packages.

JAVA_OPTS=-Xms256m -Xmx1g is now set explicitly. The start scripts use
their own default only when JAVA_OPTS is unset, and the old base always
set it, so the listeners keep the heap they have always run with. The
sdnc user keeps uid 100 / gid 102, now pinned explicitly instead of
depending on the order of system users in the base image.

Other differences:
- The image no longer inherits the old base's "java -jar /app/app.jar"
ENTRYPOINT, which could not work (there is no /app/app.jar); temurin's
default applies. OOM sets the start script as the command for
ueb-listener; dmaap-listener is not deployed by OOM.
- WORKDIR is / instead of /app. The start scripts cd to their own
directory.
- /opt/java is owned by root instead of sdnc; nothing writes to the JDK
or its cacerts at runtime. The onap user and /var/log/onap are not
created in the image.

Checked with installation/src/test/docker/image-contract.sh: all 17
listener checks pass. image-tree-diff.sh shows no difference under
/opt/onap compared with the images built from master. The start scripts
behave as before without configuration. ueb-listener stops with the
same NullPointerException. dmaap-listener fails in both old and new
images with NoClassDefFoundError javax/annotation/Priority, which is an
existing defect.

Bump the maven-patch-updates group across 1 directory with 4 updates

Bumps the maven-patch-updates group with 4 updates in the / directory: com.networknt:json-schema-validator, org.bouncycastle:bcpkix-fips, org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable and org.jruby:jruby-core.

Updates `com.networknt:json-schema-validator` from 3.0.7 to 3.0.8
## Release notes

Sourced from com.networknt:json-schema-validator's releases.

3.0.8- 2026-09-30
Added
Changed

Expose Error.isCustomMessage() to identify messages supplied by the schema through the configured error message keyword, while preserving the existing Error constructor's binary compatibility and JSON serialization format. (680d7b3, f8c7659)
Reject leading or interior empty labels and names consisting only of label separators in the idn-hostname format (#1274) Thanks @​dngr2
Allow apostrophes in uri-template literals (#1275) Thanks @​dngr2

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).

Changed

Custom validators, including overrides calling super, receive these exact values; validation uses hook results without further rounding. Integral dividend scales can change (for example, 2.0 becomes 2), which affects scale-sensitive comparisons in overrides. Mixed integral/Double or Float inputs above 2^53 can produce different results. Precision already lost when parsing floating-point values is tracked separately in #1293. (#1286)

Keep container and direct-schema caches separate so direct registry loads retain normal diagnostics regardless of registry load order, including rejection by DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory. Within one schema, a whole-document reference following a JSON Pointer reference can still reuse the container and suppress root diagnostics, including strict-factory rejection. Apply the container annotation fallback after nullable/discriminator special handling and make the container marker volatile. (#1325)
Treat unknown document-root fields as annotations when loading a schema by JSON Pointer fragment, while preserving known keyword processing and diagnostics in subschemas. With DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory, such fragment loads now succeed instead of throwing on unknown root fields; direct document loads still throw. If the selected schema references the root with $ref: "#", unknown root fields also remain annotations and do not reach the unknown-keyword factory. (#1205)

Unresolved $ref, $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef errors return internal.unresolvedRef instead of Reference {0} cannot be resolved. ## Changelog

Sourced from com.networknt:json-schema-validator's changelog.

Change Log
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
This format is based on Keep a Changelog.
This project does not adhere to Semantic Versioning and minor version changes can have incompatible API changes. These incompatible API changes will largely affect those who have custom validator or walker implementations. Those who just use the library to validate using the standard JSON Schema Draft specifications may not need changes.
[Unreleased]
Added

Opt-in ExecutionConfig.maxEvaluationSteps and maxEvaluationDepth limits for validation and schema walking, including walking without assertions. Exhaustion throws ValidationLimitExceededException instead of returning a partial validity result. Both limits default to unlimited; they bound admitted evaluation steps and schema frames, not work inside a keyword. (#1276)

Changed

MultipleOfValidator.getDivisor and getDividend now preserve exact integral and BigDecimal values. Custom validators, including overrides calling super, receive these exact values; validation uses hook results without further rounding. Integral dividend scales can change (for example, 2.0 becomes 2), which affects scale-sensitive comparisons in overrides. Mixed integral/Double or Float inputs above 2^53 can produce different results. Precision already lost when parsing floating-point values is tracked separately in #1293. (#1286)
Extend document-root unknown-keyword suppression to external $ref JSON Pointer targets. Keep container and direct-schema caches separate so direct registry loads retain normal diagnostics regardless of registry load order, including rejection by DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory. Within one schema, a whole-document reference following a JSON Pointer reference can still reuse the container and suppress root diagnostics, including strict-factory rejection. Apply the container annotation fallback after nullable/discriminator special handling and make the container marker volatile. (#1325)
Treat unknown document-root fields as annotations when loading a schema by JSON Pointer fragment, while preserving known keyword processing and diagnostics in subschemas. With DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory, such fragment loads now succeed instead of throwing on unknown root fields; direct document loads still throw. If the selected schema references the root with $ref: "#", unknown root fields also remain annotations and do not reach the unknown-keyword factory. (#1205)
Unlimited validation/walking bypasses execution counters and keeps the original recursion frame structure. During an active limited execution, reentrant convenience calls share the budget and the caller's evaluation path; unlimited calls retain their legacy root-path initialization.
Exhausted contexts reject public errors/annotation access. Walk listeners can inspect ExecutionContext.isEvaluationAborted() and getEvaluationAbort() during cleanup; an empty error slice after abort is not a validity verdict. Subclass builders supporting limits must use the protected builder constructor or forward both limits explicitly, since the legacy seven-argument constructor remains unlimited.
Error.getMessageKey() now returns the message key when the schema supplies a custom message, such as type or required, instead of the custom message text. Unresolved $ref, $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef errors return internal.unresolvedRef instead of Reference {0} cannot be resolved. Use getMessage() for the text and isCustomMessage() to detect custom messages. Errors created without a key still use their message pattern as the key. (#1319)

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

[Unreleased]
Added

Exhaustion throws ValidationLimitExceededException instead of returning a partial validity result. Changed

MultipleOfValidator.getDivisor and getDividend now preserve exact integral and BigDecimal values. Custom validators, including overrides calling super, receive these exact values; validation uses hook results without further rounding. Extend document-root unknown-keyword suppression to external $ref JSON Pointer targets. Keep container and direct-schema caches separate so direct registry loads retain normal diagnostics regardless of registry load order, including rejection by DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory. Apply the container annotation fallback after nullable/discriminator special handling and make the container marker volatile. (#1325)
Treat unknown document-root fields as annotations when loading a schema by JSON Pointer fragment, while preserving known keyword processing and diagnostics in subschemas. ## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).

Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

## Changelog

Sourced from com.networknt:json-schema-validator's changelog.

Change Log
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
This format is based on Keep a Changelog.
This project does not adhere to Semantic Versioning and minor version changes can have incompatible API changes. These incompatible API changes will largely affect those who have custom validator or walker implementations. Those who just use the library to validate using the standard JSON Schema Draft specifications may not need changes.
[Unreleased]
Added

Opt-in ExecutionConfig.maxEvaluationSteps and maxEvaluationDepth limits for validation and schema walking, including walking without assertions. Exhaustion throws ValidationLimitExceededException instead of returning a partial validity result. Both limits default to unlimited; they bound admitted evaluation steps and schema frames, not work inside a keyword. (#1276)

Changed

Ignore zero multipleOf divisors returned by custom validators, regardless of scale, matching the default conversion. (#1328)
Display multipleOf divisors in error messages using plain notation when it fits within 32 characters or is no longer than BigDecimal.toString(), including values returned by custom validators. Check the length before expanding to plain notation to avoid excessive padding for extreme scales. (#1328)
MultipleOfValidator.getDivisor and getDividend now preserve exact integral and BigDecimal values. Custom validators, including overrides calling super, receive these exact values; validation uses hook results without further rounding. Integral dividend scales can change (for example, 2.0 becomes 2), which affects scale-sensitive comparisons in overrides. Mixed integral/Double or Float inputs above 2^53 can produce different results. Precision already lost when parsing floating-point values is tracked separately in #1293. (#1286)
Extend document-root unknown-keyword suppression to external $ref JSON Pointer targets. Keep container and direct-schema caches separate so direct registry loads retain normal diagnostics regardless of registry load order, including rejection by DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory. Within one schema, a whole-document reference following a JSON Pointer reference can still reuse the container and suppress root diagnostics, including strict-factory rejection. Apply the container annotation fallback after nullable/discriminator special handling and make the container marker volatile. (#1325)
Treat unknown document-root fields as annotations when loading a schema by JSON Pointer fragment, while preserving known keyword processing and diagnostics in subschemas. With DisallowUnknownKeywordFactory, such fragment loads now succeed instead of throwing on unknown root fields; direct document loads still throw. If the selected schema references the root with $ref: "#", unknown root fields also remain annotations and do not reach the unknown-keyword factory. (#1205)
Unlimited validation/walking bypasses execution counters and keeps the original recursion frame structure. During an active limited execution, reentrant convenience calls share the budget and the caller's evaluation path; unlimited calls retain their legacy root-path initialization.
Exhausted contexts reject public errors/annotation access. Walk listeners can inspect ExecutionContext.isEvaluationAborted() and getEvaluationAbort() during cleanup; an empty error slice after abort is not a validity verdict. Subclass builders supporting limits must use the protected builder constructor or forward both limits explicitly, since the legacy seven-argument constructor remains unlimited.
Error.getMessageKey() now returns the message key when the schema supplies a custom message, such as type or required, instead of the custom message text. Unresolved $ref, $dynamicRef and $recursiveRef errors return internal.unresolvedRef instead of Reference {0} cannot be resolved. Use getMessage() for the text and isCustomMessage() to detect custom messages. Errors created without a key still use their message pattern as the key. (#1319)

old_description:
[SDC] 13.4.0

- update sdc images (1.18.0 -> 1.19-20260926T130520Z)
- stop exporting a trace for every health check
- allow WORKFLOW and NETWORK_CALL_FLOW as informational service artifacts
- size the JVM heaps from the container memory limit
- raise the sdc-be CPU limit of the small flavor from 1 to 2

Health-check polling accounts for nearly all of the trace volume the three
SDC Java services produce. Measured over one identical 10 minute window on
an idle cluster:

sdc-fe 380 / 380 traces (100%), 620 / 620 spans
sdc-be 540 / 678 traces (80%), 2456 / 8426 spans
sdc-onboarding-be 220 / 220 traces (100%), 1278 / 1278 spans

Every poll becomes its own trace: sdc-fe calls the sdc-be and onboarding
health checks every 5 seconds, sdc-be's HealthCheckScheduledTask and
JanusGraphClient's health check each run every 3 seconds, and kubelet
probes all three. Real user activity is a rounding error next to this, and
the collector and its backing store carry the whole load.

The exclusion cannot be expressed with OTEL_* variables. The agent's
ConfigurableSamplerProvider SPI exposes only the built-in samplers plus
jaeger_remote and links_parent_always_on, and the agent has no
URL-exclusion property - its only such option,
otel.instrumentation.opentelemetry-annotations.exclude-methods, would
merely remove the wrapper span and leave the calls underneath as
parentless traces. RuleBasedRoutingSampler is bundled in the agent, but
only reachable as a declarative-configuration component, so each service
now mounts an otel-config.yaml and points OTEL_CONFIG_FILE at it.

Naming a config file makes the agent ignore every other OTEL_* variable,
so exporter, sampler, service name and propagators move into the file and
the corresponding env vars go away. OTEL_ENABLED stays: it is what
startup.sh tests before attaching the agent.

The rules drop the root of each polling chain rather than the health-check
span in each service. A dropped span takes its children with it and
propagates an unsampled traceparent, so dropping sdc-be's scheduled task
also removes the four spans sdc-onboarding-be reports underneath it. This
matters because the sampler sits under parent_based, which consults the
rules for root spans only - filtering in sdc-onboarding-be alone would
leave the 90% of its traces that arrive with a sampled parent from sdc-be
untouched.

Two details worth knowing when changing these files:

- the propagator block is not optional. Unlike the environment variable
form, declarative configuration does not default to W3C propagation;
omitting it leaves the agent injecting no traceparent at all, which
silently splits every cross-service trace into single-service traces.
- a missing or malformed config file is not fatal. The agent logs a
ConfigurationException and records nothing, so the failure mode is lost
traces rather than a service that will not start.

Verified against the pinned agent (2.26.1, from the running
sdc-onboarding-be image) driven by the rendered chart config, with the
span shapes taken from the live traces. Health-check spans are dropped on
all three kinds - SERVER paths (via a genuinely instrumented HTTP server,
so url.path is proven to be available at sampling time), the CLIENT calls
sdc-fe and sdc-be make, and the two @WithSpan scheduled tasks - while
catalog requests and the Cassandra queries they make are still sampled.

sdc-be keeps the rules for its background polls from OOM-3401 (the
ApplicationDataTypeCache refresh and the sdctitan.systemlog and
sdcrepository.operationalenvironment queries). The merged file was run
through agent 2.26.1 against a real Cassandra: all five background roots
and the health-check SERVER span are dropped, while a background query on
another table and a catalog request with its 9 spans are exported.

Saving the Management Workflow or Network Call Flow tab of a service
fails with SVC4122 "Invalid artifact type". The tabs upload WORKFLOW and
NETWORK_CALL_FLOW artifacts as INFORMATIONAL, but the per-type artifact
configuration introduced in 2020 only allowed WORKFLOW as DEPLOYMENT and
gave NETWORK_CALL_FLOW no category or component type at all.

The heaps were fixed with -Xmx/-Xms, so they did not follow the flavor:
on large, sdc-be ran a 1.5G heap in a 6Gi container and sdc-fe/wfd-fe
256m in 2Gi. sdc-be and sdc-onboarding-be now use 75% of the limit and
the two Jetty frontends 50%, since their old generation holds only
10-60M after 40h and metaspace plus the otel agent need the rest of a
1Gi container. Initial equals max to keep the previous fully committed
heap. Measured on gating (cgroup v1, all JDKs detect the limit).

sdc-wfd-be keeps its fixed heap: its image ships JDK 11.0.13, which
cannot read cgroup v2 limits (added in 11.0.16) and would size a
percentage heap from node memory. Its memory request is raised to the
limit, because the fixed 1.5G heap was larger than the 1.2Gi request.

sdc-be's CPU limit on the small flavor goes from 1 to 2, request
unchanged. Its JVM start is CPU-bound against the old limit: on gating,
cadvisor showed the container throttled in 89-95% of CFS periods for the
whole 2m17s start, while the JVM sees all 8 node cores. Every other SDC
consumer waits for this start - the onap-sdc-be normatives Job only
begins once the deployment is ready - so it sits directly on the
deployment's critical path. The normatives import that follows is mostly
waiting on Cassandra (throttled in under 25% of periods), so it gains
little.

health checks every 5 seconds, sdc-be's HealthCheckScheduledTask and
JanusGraphClient's health check each run every 3 seconds, and kubelet
probes all three. Real user activity is a rounding error next to this, and
the collector and its backing store carry the whole load.

The exclusion cannot be expressed with OTEL_* variables. The agent's
ConfigurableSamplerProvider SPI exposes only the built-in samplers plus
jaeger_remote and links_parent_always_on, and the agent has no
URL-exclusion property - its only such option,
otel.instrumentation.opentelemetry-annotations.exclude-methods, would
merely remove the wrapper span and leave the calls underneath as
parentless traces. RuleBasedRoutingSampler is bundled in the agent, but
only reachable as a declarative-configuration component, so each service
now mounts an otel-config.yaml and points OTEL_CONFIG_FILE at it.

Naming a config file makes the agent ignore every other OTEL_* variable,
so exporter, sampler, service name and propagators move into the file and
the corresponding env vars go away. OTEL_ENABLED stays: it is what
startup.sh tests before attaching the agent.

The rules drop the root of each polling chain rather than the health-check
span in each service. A dropped span takes its children with it and
propagates an unsampled traceparent, so dropping sdc-be's scheduled task
also removes the four spans sdc-onboarding-be reports underneath it. This
matters because the sampler sits under parent_based, which consults the
rules for root spans only - filtering in sdc-onboarding-be alone would
leave the 90% of its traces that arrive with a sampled parent from sdc-be
untouched.

Two details worth knowing when changing these files:

- the propagator block is not optional. Unlike the environment variable
form, declarative configuration does not default to W3C propagation;
omitting it leaves the agent injecting no traceparent at all, which
silently splits every cross-service trace into single-service traces.
- a missing or malformed config file is not fatal. The agent logs a
ConfigurationException and records nothing, so the failure mode is lost
traces rather than a service that will not start.

Verified against the pinned agent (2.26.1, from the running
sdc-onboarding-be image) driven by the rendered chart config, with the
span shapes taken from the live traces. Health-check spans are dropped on
all three kinds - SERVER paths (via a genuinely instrumented HTTP server,
so url.path is proven to be available at sampling time), the CLIENT calls
sdc-fe and sdc-be make, and the two @WithSpan scheduled tasks - while
catalog requests and the Cassandra queries they make are still sampled.

sdc-be keeps the rules for its background polls from OOM-3401 (the
ApplicationDataTypeCache refresh and the sdctitan.systemlog and
sdcrepository.operationalenvironment queries). The merged file was run
through agent 2.26.1 against a real Cassandra: all five background roots
and the health-check SERVER span are dropped, while a background query on
another table and a catalog request with its 9 spans are exported.

Saving the Management Workflow or Network Call Flow tab of a service
fails with SVC4122 "Invalid artifact type". The tabs upload WORKFLOW and
NETWORK_CALL_FLOW artifacts as INFORMATIONAL, but the per-type artifact
configuration introduced in 2020 only allowed WORKFLOW as DEPLOYMENT and
gave NETWORK_CALL_FLOW no category or component type at all.

The heaps were fixed with -Xmx/-Xms, so they did not follow the flavor:
on large, sdc-be ran a 1.5G heap in a 6Gi container and sdc-fe/wfd-fe
256m in 2Gi. sdc-be and sdc-onboarding-be now use 75% of the limit and
the two Jetty frontends 50%, since their old generation holds only
10-60M after 40h and metaspace plus the otel agent need the rest of a
1Gi container. Initial equals max to keep the previous fully committed
heap. Measured on gating (cgroup v1, all JDKs detect the limit).

sdc-wfd-be keeps its fixed heap: its image ships JDK 11.0.13, which
cannot read cgroup v2 limits (added in 11.0.16) and would size a
percentage heap from node memory. Its memory request is raised to the
limit, because the fixed 1.5G heap was larger than the 1.2Gi request.

sdc-be's CPU limit on the small flavor goes from 1 to 2, request
unchanged. Its JVM start is CPU-bound against the old limit: on gating,
cadvisor showed the container throttled in 89-95% of CFS periods for the
whole 2m17s start, while the JVM sees all 8 node cores. Every other SDC
consumer waits for this start - the onap-sdc-be normatives Job only
begins once the deployment is ready - so it sits directly on the
deployment's critical path. The normatives import that follows is mostly
waiting on Cassandra (throttled in under 25% of periods), so it gains
little.

Creating a VF takes 1.9 s in sdc-be, and 1.5 s of that is idle. The
request makes three locked JanusGraph commits (the resource name lock,
the resource write and the servlet filter commit), and after writing its
lock claims each one sleeps storage.lock.wait-time before reading them
back. Cassandra work is about 350 ms of the request. Checkout, checkin,
updates and the normatives import pay the same 500 ms on every locked
commit; in the import it was 36% of the time.

The 500 ms came into effect in SDC-4904, together with moving reads from
ONE to LOCAL_QUORUM. The lost-write signature that fixed ("expected=[]
vs actual=[...]") is what a verification read served by a replica that
has not seen the lock claim produces, and quorum reads against ALL
writes rule that out. With that overlap the wait only has to cover clock
skew between the sdc-be replicas and the latency of a competing claim
that is still in flight, a few ms inside the cluster, so the JanusGraph
default of 100 ms is enough. sdc-cs keeps 500: it only creates the
schema and takes no part in this locking.

form, declarative configuration does not default to W3C propagation;

silently splits every cross-service trace into single-service traces.

gave NETWORK_CALL_FLOW no category or component type at all.

mesh. The image also writes its logs to stdout as JSON instead of to
files under /var/log/ONAP.

sdc-be's CPU limit on the small flavor goes from 1 to 2, request
unchanged. Its JVM start is CPU-bound against the old limit: on gating,
cadvisor showed the container throttled in 89-95% of CFS periods for the
whole 2m17s start, while the JVM sees all 8 node cores. Every other SDC
consumer waits for this start - the onap-sdc-be normatives Job only
begins once the deployment is ready - so it sits directly on the
deployment's critical path. The normatives import that follows is mostly
waiting on Cassandra (throttled in under 25% of periods), so it gains
little.

request makes three locked JanusGraph commits (the resource name lock,
the resource write and the servlet filter commit), and after writing its

back. Cassandra work is about 350 ms of the request. Checkout, checkin,
updates and the normatives import pay the same 500 ms on every locked
commit; in the import it was 36% of the time.

stores its value in the keyspace, and every later instance logs "Local
setting storage.lock.wait-time=PT0.1S (Type: GLOBAL_OFFLINE) is
overridden by globally managed value (PT0.5S)" and uses the stored one.

stored value; it only changes through the JanusGraph management API with

form, declarative configuration does not default to W3C propagation;
omitting it leaves the agent injecting no traceparent at all, which
silently splits every cross-service trace into single-service traces.
- a missing or malformed config file is not fatal. The agent logs a
ConfigurationException and records nothing, so the failure mode is lost
traces rather than a service that will not start.

Verified against the pinned agent (2.26.1, from the running
sdc-onboarding-be image) driven by the rendered chart config, with the
span shapes taken from the live traces. Health-check spans are dropped on
all three kinds - SERVER paths (via a genuinely instrumented HTTP server,
so url.path is proven to be available at sampling time), the CLIENT calls
sdc-fe and sdc-be make, and the two @WithSpan scheduled tasks - while
catalog requests and the Cassandra queries they make are still sampled.

sdc-be keeps the rules for its background polls from OOM-3401 (the
ApplicationDataTypeCache refresh and the sdctitan.systemlog and
sdcrepository.operationalenvironment queries). The merged file was run
through agent 2.26.1 against a real Cassandra: all five background roots
and the health-check SERVER span are dropped, while a background query on
another table and a catalog request with its 9 spans are exported.

The heaps were fixed with -Xmx/-Xms, so they did not follow the flavor:
on large, sdc-be ran a 1.5G heap in a 6Gi container and sdc-fe/wfd-fe
256m in 2Gi. sdc-be and sdc-onboarding-be now use 75% of the limit and
the two Jetty frontends 50%, since their old generation holds only
10-60M after 40h and metaspace plus the otel agent need the rest of a
1Gi container. Initial equals max to keep the previous fully committed
heap. Measured on gating (cgroup v1, all JDKs detect the limit).

sdc-wfd-be follows sdc-be at 75%. Its 1.15 image moves from JDK 11.0.13,
which cannot read cgroup v2 limits (added in 11.0.16), to Temurin
17.0.20, which sizes a 2Gi limit to the same 1536m heap the fixed -Xmx
gave. Its memory request is raised to the limit, because that heap was
larger than the 1.2Gi request.

The 1.15 workflow backend replaces Sleuth/Zipkin with the OpenTelemetry
Spring Boot starter, which reads the standard OTEL_* variables and no
longer reads TRACING_*. It exports OTLP over HTTP only (the JDK sender;
okhttp's gRPC sender cannot run on Boot 2.7's Kotlin), so the chart
points it at port 4318 and gets an otlpHttp port like the cds charts.
OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is the inverse of global.tracing.enabled, tracing stays
off by default, and the skip pattern goes away because the image drops
/actuator requests in its own sampler. SDC_PROTOCOL is gone too: the
backend now always calls sdc-be over plain HTTP and leaves TLS to the
mesh. The image also writes its logs to stdout as JSON instead of to
files under /var/log/ONAP.

sdc-be's CPU limit on the small flavor goes from 1 to 2, request
unchanged. Its JVM start is CPU-bound against the old limit: on gating,
cadvisor showed the container throttled in 89-95% of CFS periods for the
whole 2m17s start, while the JVM sees all 8 node cores. Every other SDC
consumer waits for this start - the onap-sdc-be normatives Job only
begins once the deployment is ready - so it sits directly on the
deployment's critical path. The normatives import that follows is mostly
waiting on Cassandra (throttled in under 25% of periods), so it gains
little.

Creating a VF takes 1.9 s in sdc-be, and 1.5 s of that is idle. The
request makes three locked JanusGraph commits (the resource name lock,
the resource write and the servlet filter commit), and after writing its
lock claims each one sleeps storage.lock.wait-time before reading them
back. Cassandra work is about 350 ms of the request. Checkout, checkin,
updates and the normatives import pay the same 500 ms on every locked
commit; in the import it was 36% of the time.

The 500 ms came into effect in SDC-4904, together with moving reads from
ONE to LOCAL_QUORUM. The lost-write signature that fixed ("expected=[]
vs actual=[...]") is what a verification read served by a replica that
has not seen the lock claim produces, and quorum reads against ALL
writes rule that out. With that overlap the wait only has to cover clock
skew between the sdc-be replicas and the latency of a competing claim
that is still in flight, a few ms inside the cluster, so the JanusGraph
default of 100 ms is enough.

The value is lowered for sdc-cs as well. storage.lock.wait-time is a
GLOBAL_OFFLINE JanusGraph option: the first instance to open the graph
stores its value in the keyspace, and every later instance logs "Local
setting storage.lock.wait-time=PT0.1S (Type: GLOBAL_OFFLINE) is
overridden by globally managed value (PT0.5S)" and uses the stored one.
That first instance is the sdc-cs schema creation, so lowering sdc-be
alone left every lock wait at 500 ms. An existing keyspace keeps its
stored value; it only changes through the JanusGraph management API with
no other instance open.

The validator bump needs the onboarding change with it. The new image
validates with the Helm it ships (Alpine's, 3.19.0) and no longer offers
3.5.2, so the 3.5.2 that onboarding asks for gets a 400, and onboarding
records that only as a warning: Helm chart validation would be skipped
without anyone noticing. v3 resolves to the newest Helm 3 the validator
has, so later validator images no longer need a matching OOM change.
