leave the 90% of its traces that arrive with a sampled parent from sdc-be
untouched.

Two details worth knowing when changing these files:

- the propagator block is not optional. Unlike the environment variable
form, declarative configuration does not default to W3C propagation;
omitting it leaves the agent injecting no traceparent at all, which
silently splits every cross-service trace into single-service traces.
- a missing or malformed config file is not fatal. The agent logs a
ConfigurationException and records nothing, so the failure mode is lost
traces rather than a service that will not start.

Verified against the pinned agent (2.26.1, from the running
sdc-onboarding-be image) driven by the rendered chart config, with the
span shapes taken from the live traces. Health-check spans are dropped on
all three kinds - SERVER paths (via a genuinely instrumented HTTP server,
so url.path is proven to be available at sampling time), the CLIENT calls
sdc-fe and sdc-be make, and the two @WithSpan scheduled tasks - while
catalog requests and the Cassandra queries they make are still sampled.

sdc-be keeps the rules for its background polls from OOM-3401 (the
ApplicationDataTypeCache refresh and the sdctitan.systemlog and
sdcrepository.operationalenvironment queries). The merged file was run
through agent 2.26.1 against a real Cassandra: all five background roots
and the health-check SERVER span are dropped, while a background query on
another table and a catalog request with its 9 spans are exported.

The heaps were fixed with -Xmx/-Xms, so they did not follow the flavor:
on large, sdc-be ran a 1.5G heap in a 6Gi container and sdc-fe/wfd-fe
256m in 2Gi. sdc-be and sdc-onboarding-be now use 75% of the limit and
the two Jetty frontends 50%, since their old generation holds only
10-60M after 40h and metaspace plus the otel agent need the rest of a
1Gi container. Initial equals max to keep the previous fully committed
heap. Measured on gating (cgroup v1, all JDKs detect the limit).

sdc-wfd-be follows sdc-be at 75%. Its 1.15 image moves from JDK 11.0.13,
which cannot read cgroup v2 limits (added in 11.0.16), to Temurin
17.0.20, which sizes a 2Gi limit to the same 1536m heap the fixed -Xmx
gave. Its memory request is raised to the limit, because that heap was
larger than the 1.2Gi request.

The 1.15 workflow backend replaces Sleuth/Zipkin with the OpenTelemetry
Spring Boot starter, which reads the standard OTEL_* variables and no
longer reads TRACING_*. It exports OTLP over HTTP only (the JDK sender;
okhttp's gRPC sender cannot run on Boot 2.7's Kotlin), so the chart
points it at port 4318 and gets an otlpHttp port like the cds charts.
OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is the inverse of global.tracing.enabled, tracing stays
off by default, and the skip pattern goes away because the image drops
/actuator requests in its own sampler. SDC_PROTOCOL is gone too: the
backend now always calls sdc-be over plain HTTP and leaves TLS to the
mesh. The image also writes its logs to stdout as JSON instead of to
files under /var/log/ONAP.

sdc-be's CPU limit on the small flavor goes from 1 to 2, request
unchanged. Its JVM start is CPU-bound against the old limit: on gating,
cadvisor showed the container throttled in 89-95% of CFS periods for the
whole 2m17s start, while the JVM sees all 8 node cores. Every other SDC
consumer waits for this start - the onap-sdc-be normatives Job only
begins once the deployment is ready - so it sits directly on the
deployment's critical path. The normatives import that follows is mostly
waiting on Cassandra (throttled in under 25% of periods), so it gains
little.

Creating a VF takes 1.9 s in sdc-be, and 1.5 s of that is idle. The
request makes three locked JanusGraph commits (the resource name lock,
the resource write and the servlet filter commit), and after writing its
lock claims each one sleeps storage.lock.wait-time before reading them
back. Cassandra work is about 350 ms of the request. Checkout, checkin,
updates and the normatives import pay the same 500 ms on every locked
commit; in the import it was 36% of the time.

The 500 ms came into effect in SDC-4904, together with moving reads from
ONE to LOCAL_QUORUM. The lost-write signature that fixed ("expected=[]
vs actual=[...]") is what a verification read served by a replica that
has not seen the lock claim produces, and quorum reads against ALL
writes rule that out. With that overlap the wait only has to cover clock
skew between the sdc-be replicas and the latency of a competing claim
that is still in flight, a few ms inside the cluster, so the JanusGraph
default of 100 ms is enough.

The value is lowered for sdc-cs as well. storage.lock.wait-time is a
GLOBAL_OFFLINE JanusGraph option: the first instance to open the graph
stores its value in the keyspace, and every later instance logs "Local
setting storage.lock.wait-time=PT0.1S (Type: GLOBAL_OFFLINE) is
overridden by globally managed value (PT0.5S)" and uses the stored one.
That first instance is the sdc-cs schema creation, so lowering sdc-be
alone left every lock wait at 500 ms. An existing keyspace keeps its
stored value; it only changes through the JanusGraph management API with
no other instance open.

The validator bump needs the onboarding change with it. The new image
validates with the Helm it ships (Alpine's, 3.19.0) and no longer offers
3.5.2, so the 3.5.2 that onboarding asks for gets a 400, and onboarding
records that only as a warning: Helm chart validation would be skipped
without anyone noticing. v3 resolves to the newest Helm 3 the validator
has, so later validator images no longer need a matching OOM change.

v2.22.3
What's Changed

Added support for Avrea-hosted runners (enterprise tier)
Fixed unexpected blocking of allowed connections caused by GitHub’s DNS resolver and outbound proxy experiment on GitHub-hosted Linux runners
Added a feature flag to disable implicit AWS endpoint allowances on self-hosted Linux runners (enterprise tier)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/compare/v2.22.2...v2.22.3
v2.22.2
What's Changed

Fixed inbound (ingress) network traffic being incorrectly classified as outbound (egress) traffic on macOS
Fixed implicit endpoints intended for self-hosted runners being applied to custom VM environments on Linux (enterprise tier)
Improved network and DNS tracing, enforcement logic, and process information correlation on Linux (enterprise tier)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/compare/v2.22.1...v2.22.2
v2.22.1
What's Changed

Fixed security rules not initializing on GHES self-hosted runners
Fixed GHES connectivity in block mode by implicitly allowing the GHES hostname

Full Changelog: https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/compare/v2.22.0...v2.22.1
v2.22.0
What's Changed

Linux ARM64 support for community tier
GHES support for self-hosted VMs (enterprise tier)
MacOS and Windows runner deny list support for block policy (enterprise tier).

Full Changelog: https://github.com/step-security/harden-runner/compare/v2.21.1...v2.22.0

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

[SO] Export so-cnf-adapter traces with Spring Boot 3 properties

Since the 1.17.1 image (Spring Boot 3.5), so-cnf-adapter ignores the
Spring Cloud Sleuth keys spring.sleuth.* and spring.zipkin.base-url the
chart still sets. Tracing falls back to the jar default
TRACING_ENABLED=false, so the adapter has exported no trace since
2026-10-28 11:03Z.

Set management.tracing.* as in so-bpmn-infra, and point
management.zipkin.tracing.endpoint at the chart's collector
(jaeger-collector.istio-config) instead of the jar default in
istio-system. The image ships the Brave bridge and the Zipkin reporter
but no OTLP exporter, so it keeps using the Zipkin port. Also disable
the Spring Security and scheduled-task observations, as OOM-3400 did
for the other SO components.

so-cnfm-lcm (1.17.1) and so-etsi-sol003-adapter (1.13.1) carry the same
Sleuth block, but their images contain no micrometer-tracing bridge, so
Boot 3 keys would not make them trace either. The dead block and the
tracing.ignorePatterns value it read are removed.

old_description:
Add OpenTelemetry tracing to the artifactbroker

A distribution arrives on the SDC distribution client's Kafka polling
thread, so nothing ties the downloads from SDC and the requests to the
k8s plugin together, and the k8s plugin cannot join its spans to the
distribution that caused them.

Add spring-boot-starter-opentelemetry and wrap every notification in an
artifactbroker.distribution observation, with one artifactbroker.download
child per artifact. The k8s plugin calls go through the auto-configured
RestClient.Builder, so they become child spans and carry a W3C
traceparent header. The existing artifactbroker_distributions_total and
artifactbroker_downloads_total counters stay as they are; the
observations add the artifactbroker_distribution_seconds and
artifactbroker_download_seconds timers.

Tracing is off by default because OOM ships no collector. The OTLP
metrics registry the starter brings is switched off: metrics are still
scraped from /actuator/prometheus.

Environment variables:
- TRACING_ENABLED (default false)
- TRACING_SAMPLING_PROBABILITY (default 1.0)
- COLLECTOR_HOST (default http://jaeger-collector.istio-system)
- COLLECTOR_PORT (default 4318, OTLP over HTTP, path /v1/traces)

Issue-ID: MULTICLOUD-1589

A distribution arrives on the SDC distribution client's Kafka polling
thread, so nothing ties the downloads from SDC and the requests to the
k8s plugin together, and the k8s plugin cannot join its spans to the
distribution that caused them.

artifactbroker.distribution observation, with one artifactbroker.download

traceparent header. The existing artifactbroker_distributions_total and
artifactbroker_downloads_total counters stay as they are; the
observations add the artifactbroker_distribution_seconds and
artifactbroker_download_seconds timers.

Tracing is off by default because OOM ships no collector. The OTLP
metrics registry the starter brings is switched off: metrics are still
scraped from /actuator/prometheus.

is prefixed with the subsystem: multicloud-framework-artifactbroker.

old_description:
k6 test: detect READY cm-handle gauge over-count in k6

The k6 kpi and endurance profiles only confirmed cm-handle convergence
once in setup, so a READY gauge that drifted above the registered total
later in the run went unnoticed.

- Query Prometheus at teardown for the peak READY gauge over the whole
run, so a transient over-count is caught even after reconciliation
resets it; the cps-path DB count cannot see this drift
- Fail the run via a dedicated threshold when the peak exceeds the
registered total, and skip cleanly when Prometheus is unavailable
- Enable Prometheus for the kpi and endurance profiles only, leaving
other installs unchanged

old_description:
CI: Scope concurrency to the Gerrit change

Every ONAP project's required workflows run in this repository, so a
concurrency group is shared across all of them. The groups keyed on the
Change-Id, which does not identify a Gerrit change: a cherry-pick to a
maintenance branch keeps it (cps change 145853 on master and 145856 on
maintenance/3.7.10 share one), and another project may reuse it.

- The merge group omitted the branch, so a change and its cherry-pick
merging close together would cancel one publication.
- doc-rules-compose carried its own group, also without the branch, so
verifying a change and its cherry-pick together cancelled one's
documentation checks. The caller already holds a group per change,
so the called workflow's group is removed rather than repaired.
- The verify groups omitted the project.

Each group now keys on the Gerrit project and change number. The
number is unique on the server and shared by every patchset of a
change, so a new patchset still supersedes the previous run while
separate changes can no longer cancel each other.

An audit of all 213 cancelled runs since 19 August found no collision
between distinct changes so far; this closes the gap before one
occurs.

The bypassable verify called doc-rules-compose pinned to an older
commit of this repository, where the change above would never take
effect. It now uses the self-repository reference, which resolves
inside the calling commit; the workflow is unchanged since that pin.

Issue-ID: CIMAN-33

old_description:
Chore: Remove Jenkins jobs that nothing can trigger

Nine job definitions serve no repository or are already switched off.
Deleting them also deletes the jobs from Jenkins on merge, because the
ci-management merge runs jenkins-jobs update --delete-old.

- rtdv3-global-verify-master and rtdv3-global-merge-master have been
disabled since 2023-09; the org-level GHA required workflows build
the docs now. The rtdv3-global view, empty without them, goes too.
- lab-tlab-oom-daily, lab-windriver-oom-daily and
lab-windriver-oom-staging-daily have no repository and no trigger,
and have not run since 2018-2019.
- openci-onap-autorelease-daily-master and
openci-onap-promote-daily-master have no repository and no trigger,
and have not run since 2018-09.
- The testsuite-cds-mock-odl docker stanza names the Gerrit project
testsuite/cds-modk-odl, which does not exist. The merge job cannot
clone it, so its weekly run on an 8-vCPU node fails; the verify job
has never run. testsuite/cds-mock-odl itself is dormant, so the
stanza is removed rather than corrected.

Rendering with JJB 6.3.0 shows exactly these nine jobs and the
rtdv3-global view gone, and no other job or view changed.

old_description:
Replace artifactbroker's policy-distribution framework with Spring Boot

artifactbroker was a fork of ONAP policy-distribution: a pluggable
reception-handler/forwarder framework on policy-common, Jersey, Jetty
and swagger 1.5, wired by class name from JSON, of which only one
handler and one forwarder were ever used. Rewrite it as a single-module
Spring Boot 4 service, structured like aai-model-loader.

- SdcConnection initializes and starts the SDC distribution client and
retries until it succeeds. Exceptions and linkage errors from the
client are caught, as a periodic task that throws is never run again.
Its health is DOWN while SDC is unreachable, but it is kept out of
the readiness group: the broker is a sidecar, and an unready broker
would take the k8s plugin out of its Service.
- NotificationHandler downloads VF_MODULES_METADATA and every artifact
its VF modules reference. It then picks each module's chart (HELM first,
then the CLOUD_TECHNOLOGY_SPECIFIC_ARTIFACT matching the module name,
unchanged), skips modules without one and registers the rest one by
one. A failure in one VF no longer stops the others. Charts stay in
memory, so /data is no longer needed.
- K8sPluginClient keeps the definition key (invariant/customization
UUID) and the reuse of an existing definition.

The wire behaviour is unchanged, including CR 148921's skipping of VF
modules without a chart. A black-box suite (kept outside the
repository) that drives the image through a stub SDC, a stub k8s plugin
and a SASL/SCRAM Kafka passes against both the previous image and this
one; only the REST-server tests differ.

Behaviour changes:
- the definition is created with "description" instead of the
misspelt "descritpion", which the k8s plugin ignored
- the chart is uploaded as application/octet-stream
- the component-done status names the component MULTICLOUD instead of
the policy-distribution leftover POLICY
- /healthcheck and /statistics are replaced by /actuator/health
(liveness, readiness) and /actuator/prometheus. OOM only uses TCP
probes, and nothing else calls the old endpoints.

kafka-clients is pinned to 3.9.1 because the SDC distribution client
is built against Kafka 3; the Boot BOM would otherwise move it to 4.
jacoco is overridden to 0.8.13 because oparent's 0.8.5 cannot read
Java 17 classes. Version bumped to 1.10.0 across the repository.

Needs the ci-management change that builds multicloud-framework with
Java 17, and an OOM change for the new configuration and probes.

- update images of main SO repo (1.21.0 -> 1.22.0-20261027T1544)
- update the SO adapter images to the SO 1.22.0 / Spring Boot 3.5.16 /
Java 21 builds:
- so-cnf-adapter, so-cnfm-as-lcm (1.16.0 -> 1.17.0-20261027T1538)
- so-etsi-nfvo-ns-lcm (1.12.0 -> 1.13.0-20261027T1539)
- so-etsi-sol003-adapter (1.12.0 -> 1.13.0-20261027T1539)
- so-etsi-sol005-adapter (1.12.0 -> 1.13.0-20261027T1539)
- so-nssmf-adapter (1.14.0 -> 1.15.0-20261027T1539)
- so-oof-adapter (1.13.0 -> 1.14.0-20261027T1540)
- export traces to the OTLP HTTP endpoint instead of Zipkin, since
the images now ship the OTLP exporter, which Spring Boot only
creates when management.otlp.tracing.endpoint is set
- introduce .global.auth.so.users to configure the SO credentials
centrally, as .global.auth.aai does for AAI. Every SO service
accepts all of these users, and SO services call each other with
the first one (so.auth.username/password). The images read plain
credentials now and hash plaintext passwords at startup, so the
per-service users, BCrypt hashes and htpasswd init steps are gone
- read the AAI credentials from .global.auth.aai.users
(aai.username/password) in every SO service
- drop the msoKey ciphertexts, pre-encoded Basic headers, mso.key /
sdc.key values and the mso-key secrets, which the images no longer
read; the SDC passwords are now set in plaintext

old_description:
Chore: Retire Sonar job stanzas migrated to GitHub Actions

WORK IN PROGRESS - do not merge. Held for TSC sign-off and for the
agreed exit criteria below.

36 repositories now run their SonarCloud analysis from GitHub Actions
and report to the same SonarCloud projects the Jenkins jobs use. This
removes the 44 now-duplicated JJB stanzas: one per repository for the
gerrit-maven-sonar branch scan, plus a second for the eight projects
that also define gerrit-maven-sonar-verify.

Only stanzas whose every job is a Sonar template are removed, and only
for repositories whose GitHub Actions lane has already merged. No
stanza that mixes Sonar with other jobs is touched, and no other job
family is affected. The change is therefore pure deletion and reverts
cleanly by restoring the file.

The replacement lanes are:

sonar-master.yaml schedule + manual dispatch, writes the
project's own branch analysis, never votes
gerrit-sonar-verify.yaml dispatched per patch set, writes a
short-lived <change>-<patchset> branch and
votes Verified

Both call lfreleng-actions/security-workflows sonarqube-cloud.yaml, so
the analyser version travels with the shared workflow rather than with
a per-project job definition.

Exit criteria agreed for this step, none of which this change asserts
are met yet:

1. the GitHub Actions lane runs green for two consecutive weeks
2. the result is visible on the Gerrit change
3. PTL sign-off for the affected projects
4. this removal lands as a separate, revertible commit

Until it merges both systems run and both report, so turning the
GitHub Actions workflow off is a complete rollback.

new_description:
Chore: Retire Sonar job stanzas migrated to GitHub Actions

36 repositories now run their SonarCloud analysis from GitHub Actions,
reporting to the same SonarCloud projects these Jenkins jobs use, so
the analysis history is continuous. This removes the 44 JJB stanzas
those lanes replace: one per repository for the gerrit-maven-sonar
branch scan, plus a second for the eight projects that also define
gerrit-maven-sonar-verify.

The replacement lanes are:

sonar-master.yaml schedule and manual dispatch, writes the
project's own branch analysis, never votes
gerrit-sonar-verify.yaml dispatched per patch set, writes a
short-lived <change>-<patchset> branch and
votes Verified

Both call sonarqube-cloud.yaml from lfreleng-actions/security-workflows,
so the analyser version travels with the shared workflow rather than
with a per-project job definition. That is the point of the move: a
fix to the scan applies once, not across forty-odd near-identical job
definitions.

Scope is deliberately narrow. A stanza is removed only when every job
it defines is a Sonar template, and only for repositories whose GitHub
Actions lane has already merged. No stanza that mixes Sonar with other
jobs is touched, and no other job family is affected. The change is
pure deletion, so restoring a file restores its jobs exactly.

old_description:
poc: run module sync only on the master instance

Proof-of-concept for CPS-3437: gate the scheduled module-sync watchdog so
only the master instance runs module sync, eliminating multi-instance
concurrency on the same cm handle (and the race that caused CPS-3435).

- Master election reuses the shared cpsCommonLocks map: first instance to
acquire the module-sync master lock becomes master; a non-master
re-attempts each cycle so a survivor takes over if the master dies.
- Only the scheduled entry point is gated; the direct method used by tests
is unchanged.
- Add feature toggle ncmp.timers.advised-modules-sync.master-only
(default false); enabled for k6/endurance via the cps-charts values.
- When enabled, only the elected master instance runs module sync;
re-election is automatic (Hazelcast frees the key lock when the master
leaves the cluster), no lock TTL needed.
- When enabled, skip the now-redundant cross-instance coordination: no
in-progress map writes, a local work queue instead of the distributed
one, and no distributed work-queue lock.
- Updated skill files for better control of test titles following our
conventions (avoid expectations in titles)

Intent: confirm a single instance keeps up at 50k (cm_handles_created stays
well above the 22/s threshold)

old_description:
Close Go stdlib and x/net CVEs for the 7.0.3 release

New advisories have landed against the go1.26.8 toolchain and
golang.org/x/net v0.56.0 since the 7.0.2 pass (INT-2408).

- bump the builder image from golang:1.26.8 to golang:1.26.10 and the
go.mod toolchain directive to match, so builds outside the Dockerfile
(CI verify) get the fix too. This closes the open standard-library
advisories in net/http, crypto/tls, crypto/x509, net/textproto, os
and html/template (GO-2026-6600, -6603, -6604, -6605, -6607, -6608,
-6609, -6610, -6611, -6612, -6613, -6617, -6809). Ten of them are
reachable through the client-go connection to the API server.
GO-2026-6809 (distrusted x509 intermediates) is only fixed in 1.26.10,
which is the current 1.26 patch and is present on the ONAP Nexus
Docker Hub proxy.
- bump golang.org/x/net v0.56.0 -> v0.60.0, closing the HTTP/2
advisories GO-2026-6603, -6610, -6611, -6612 and -6617 in the
x/net/http2 copy that client-go links.
- golang.org/x/text moves v0.39.0 -> v0.42.0, which also closes
GO-2026-6629 (x/text/secure/precis, not linked). golang.org/x/sys and
golang.org/x/term move to v0.48.0 and v0.46.0, because the x/*
modules require each other in lockstep.

x/net v0.60.0 declares go 1.26.0, so the go directive moves from 1.25.0
to 1.26.0. The toolchain and builder were already on 1.26, so this
changes the language level but no build environment. v0.60.0 is the
fixed version; v0.61.0 (latest) was deliberately not taken.

govulncheck ./... now reports "No vulnerabilities found". The
module-level scan over the full build list leaves 3 findings
(moby/spdystream, yuin/goldmark, x/crypto/openpgp). All 3 are in
modules absent from go.mod, with no linked packages and "main module
does not need module", so they neither ship nor gate a dir-SBOM scan.

No functional change to the readiness logic.

old_description:
[COMMON] Remove the envsubst init containers and image

Charts substituted ${VAR} placeholders into config files with a
dibi/envsubst:latest init container that copied them to an emptyDir.
The image is an unpinned latest tag with known vulnerabilities. Replace
it without another runtime templating step:

- Apps that resolve ${VAR} from the environment themselves get the
ConfigMap mounted directly and the variables on the main container:
policy-api, policy-pap, clamp-runtime-acm, cps-core, cps-temporal,
ncmp-dmi-plugin, cds-blueprints-processor and uui-server (Spring
Boot), sdnc, its dbinit job and ueb-listener (SLI EnvProperties,
DBResourceManager, SDNR config, oauth Config), dgbuilder
(customSettings.js now uses process.env, copied to an emptyDir so
the settings UI can still write it) and drools-pdp (base.conf is
sourced by the shell; the JAAS quote stripping moves to the main
container). uui needs no substitution at all.
- apex-pdp and xacml-pdp only resolve the REST server credentials
from env. Their Kafka settings are rendered by Helm, the JAAS config
is read from the mounted KafkaUser secret by Kafka's
DirectoryConfigProvider and xacml's per-pod group.id by the
EnvVarConfigProvider (kafka-clients 4.x in the 5.0.1 images).
- Credentials owned by the chart that the app reads verbatim are
rendered into a Secret with the new
common.secret.renderedValueFast helper, which fails if the secret is
configured as externalSecret: xacml-pdp and distribution client
credentials, the a1policymanagement controller (copied to an emptyDir
so PUT /configuration keeps working; the inotify sidecar is replaced
by a checksum annotation) and the oom-cert-service test cmpServers.
xacml.properties carries the policy DB credentials, which are derived
in the policy chart, so the policy chart renders it.
- The crunchy postgres image already runs envsubst on /pgconf/setup.sql

old_description:
[PMSH] Pin Werkzeug so that Flask 2.2 can start

setup.py pins Flask==2.2 but not Werkzeug, and Flask 2.2 accepts
any Werkzeug >= 2.2.0. Since Werkzeug 3.0 (2023-09) a fresh install
resolves Werkzeug 3.x, which removed werkzeug.urls.url_quote, so
`import flask` fails:

ImportError: cannot import name 'url_quote' from 'werkzeug.urls'

Every image or tox run built since then therefore fails at import
time. Pin Werkzeug to 2.2.3, the last release of the line Flask 2.2
was built against.

On Python 3.9, a clean install of master fails test collection with
the error above. With this pin, all 141 tests pass (90% coverage).

Issue-ID: DCAEGEN2-3463
new_description:
[PMSH] Fix image build and startup

The pmsh image has not built since mid-2023, and an image built today
crashes at startup. Most declared dependencies are pinned, but the
unpinned transitive ones have moved on. Four separate problems:

- setup.py pins Flask==2.2 but not Werkzeug, so Werkzeug 3.x resolves.
It removed werkzeug.urls.url_quote, and `import flask` fails with an
ImportError. Pin Werkzeug==2.2.3.
- pyyaml 5.4.1 has no wheel for musl or Python 3.10, and its sdist
does not build with Cython 3 ('build_ext' object has no attribute
'cython_sources'). This fails both the docker build and tox.
Moving to pyyaml 6 is not an option, because onappylog 1.0.9 (the
latest release) calls yaml.load() without a Loader. Instead, build
pyyaml with Cython < 3 through build-constraints.txt, passed as
PIP_CONSTRAINT (pip 21 in the image) and as PIP_BUILD_CONSTRAINT
(pip 25.3+, which Jenkins tox uses and which no longer applies
PIP_CONSTRAINT to isolated builds).
- SQLAlchemy 2.x (unpinned through Flask-SQLAlchemy) imports greenlet.
greenlet 3.2+ ships musllinux_1_2 wheels that segfault on import on
the Alpine 3.15 base image. Pin greenlet==3.1.1, the last release
with a musllinux_1_1 wheel.
- connexion 2.5.0 imports pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removed.
The image's setuptools 58 is fine, but tox venvs get the latest
setuptools. Declare setuptools<82.

tox also failed to collect tests: {toxinidir} was not on PYTHONPATH,
so `tests.base_setup` resolved to an installed `tests` package
(pmsh's own, installed without its data files, or onappylog's stray
one). Add {toxinidir} to the front of PYTHONPATH.

The Jenkins copyright check also requires a current-year copyright
line in each modified file it checks.

Verified:
- `tox -e py310,flake8` on python:3.10 with pip 26.2: 141 passed,
coverage 90%
- the docker build succeeds, and the container starts against a
Postgres, creates its 6 tables, and stops only at the missing
CONFIG_BINDING_SERVICE

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). ## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

New Contributors

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme

old_description:
Build sdnc-image on eclipse-temurin instead of ccsdk-odlsli

Today sdnc-image sits at the end of a chain of base images. Three of
them are released separately from ccsdk/distribution:

eclipse-temurin -> ccsdk-alpine-j21-image
-> ccsdk-odl-titanium-alpine-image -> ccsdk-odlsli-alpine-image
-> sdnc-image

The last three steps (odl-titanium, odlsli and sdnc-image itself) each
end with FROM scratch + COPY / /, so sdnc-image is a single 1.8 GB
layer and the upstream image underneath can't be seen. A fix in the
JDK, in Alpine or in SLI only reaches SDNC after it has gone through
these releases:

JDK/Alpine fix: alpine-j21 release -> odl-titanium release ->
odlsli release -> version bump + sdnc/oam release
SLI fix: sli release -> odlsli release ->
version bump + sdnc/oam release

In practice this happens rarely. The released sdnc-image:3.2.4 still
runs Alpine 3.21.3, and on master the chain is currently stuck:
- Since merge-verification #212, the base tag 2.3.0-SNAPSHOT-latest is
gone from nexus3 (404), and odlsli cannot publish a new one, because
its pom tags with *.snapshot.version properties that TagVersion.groovy
never sets.
- The rsync step in odlsli and in this Dockerfile fails with the rsync
3.5.0 in current Alpine ("Symbolic link loop", because $ODL_HOME is
the symlink /opt/opendaylight/current).
- odlsli takes SLI from a version range, so sdnc-image contains
whatever SLI was newest when odlsli was built, not the
ccsdk.sli.version this repo pins. 3.2.4 pins SLI 2.2.1 but boots
2.2.2-SNAPSHOT. Local odlsli builds of the same master commit gave
2.3.0 one day and 2.3.1-SNAPSHOT the next.
- With SLI 2.3.0 the image does not boot. Karaf logs "Error installing
boot features", because ccsdk-sli 2.3.0 pins guava 33.4.0-jre,
commons-lang3 3.17.0 and others that are not in the Titanium system
repository. On master, the sdnc CSIT plan timed out at Karaf start in
#210 and #211. A local build of master shows the boot-feature error.

With this change sdnc/oam builds the image itself in an "assemble"
stage. The inputs are Maven artifacts only, no ccsdk/distribution
image:
- org.opendaylight.integration:onap-karaf:0.22.1 (tar.gz), the ODL
distribution that ccsdk-odl-titanium-alpine-image unpacks
- the 27 CCSDK SLI *-installer zips at ${ccsdk.sli.version}, plus the
distribution "dependencies" and "platform-logic-installer" zips at
${ccsdk.distribution.version}
- the /opt/onap/ccsdk files and the pax-logging config that the odlsli
image added. They are copied verbatim from ccsdk/distribution 5094897
odlsli/src/main/{scripts,resources,properties,stores} into
installation/sdnc/src/main/ccsdk. From now on sdnc/oam owns these
copies.

The final stage is FROM eclipse-temurin:21.0.12.1_1-jre-alpine
(java.base.image in the root pom), not FROM scratch. It installs only
the tools the SDNC scripts call and copies /opt/opendaylight, /opt/onap
and /opt/opentelemetry from the assemble stage. It also runs apk
upgrade. A pinned temurin tag stops being rebuilt once the next JDK is
out, and its Alpine packages then age: the previously used
21.0.10_7-jre-alpine was last rebuilt in April and still has libexpat
2.7.5, while Alpine ships 2.9.0. With apk upgrade, every rebuild picks
up the current Alpine fixes even if the tag itself is old.

What this changes:
- Fewer releases. No ccsdk/distribution image release is in the path
any more; the two distribution zips are plain Maven dependencies. A
JDK or Alpine fix needs a rebuild of sdnc/oam or a one-line
java.base.image bump. An SLI fix needs an sli release and a
ccsdk.sli.version bump.
- The image contains exactly the SLI version this repo pins (today
2.3.1-SNAPSHOT; with a release pin the image is reproducible), never a
range. Karaf installs its boot features again.
- CVEs (Trivy, one run with the same DB, 2026-10-23):

critical high medium low
sdnc-image 3.2.4 30 240 311 91
master, local build (*) 18 87 120 62
this change 16 74 90 12

(*) built locally with the rsync step patched; CI cannot build it.
The jar findings of that build are the same as in this change, so the
whole difference from master is in OS packages, which go from
14/163/211/75 in 3.2.4 to zero. The critical findings that are gone
include CVE-2026-31789 (openssl), CVE-2026-33845 and CVE-2026-42010
(gnutls), CVE-2026-44170 and CVE-2026-44172 (mariadb client),
CVE-2025-55130 and CVE-2026-48930 (nodejs) and CVE-2025-3277
(sqlite). All remaining findings are in Java jars (ODL, CCSDK
SLI/SDNR, AAF and the OpenTelemetry agent) and do not depend on the
base image. The OpenTelemetry agent (2.24.0, CVE-2026-33701, fixed in
2.26.1) can be bumped in a follow-up.
- JDK 21.0.12.1 instead of 21.0.10 in the current chain.
- 3.2.4 -> this change: 1.81 GB -> 1.24 GB, 158 -> 97 apk packages.
nodejs, npm, git, sudo, graphviz, pip and rsync are gone, and so is
the 195 MB /tmp/system left behind by the old rsync step.
- The temurin layers stay separate, so scanners can see the base and
nodes share it with other temurin images.
- curl and jq are installed. They were missing in 3.2.4, although
backupMdsal.sh, restoreMdsal.sh, switchVoting.sh and sdnc.cluster
call them.

Unchanged for deployments: user odl with uid 100 / gid 102 (existing
volumes stay writable), the startODL.sh entrypoint, WORKDIR, EXPOSE
8181, the /opt layout, the SDNC environment variables, keystores, and
the ONAP CA in the JDK truststore. No OOM chart change is needed. OOM
mounts /var/log/onap itself. Rollback is a revert or pinning the image
back to 3.2.4; the PVC data stays compatible.

Differences an operator may notice:
- odl is no longer in "wheel" and sudo is not installed (no script uses
it).
- /opt, /opt/sdnc and /opt/java (including cacerts) are owned by root;
nothing writes to them at runtime.
- The onap user (1000:101), the empty /opt/odl and /var/log/onap are no
longer created in the image.
- temurin's PATH (JDK first), LANG, LANGUAGE and JAVA_VERSION apply.

How this was checked: installation/src/test/docker/image-contract.sh
checks 51 properties of an image: base layers, user ids, required and
unwanted tools, Java 21, paths and ownership, the ONAP CA, the
JndiLookup removal, the boot features, the exact SLI version in
featuresRepositories, and the Highstreet patch jars against Maven
Central. All 51 pass for sdnc-image and sdnc-aaf-image. 3.2.4 differs
in 12. Seven of those are the intended changes (base layers, no node,
npm, git, sudo, dot, pip3), and the others are the defects above:
curl and jq missing, the /tmp/system leftover, SLI 2.2.2-SNAPSHOT
instead of the pinned 2.2.1, and the AAA patch in an unused version
directory. image-tree-diff.sh compares mode, owner and path of every
file under /opt, with version numbers normalised, against the image of
the previous change (built locally with the rsync step patched). It
finds 61 added maven-metadata-local.xml files, which SNAPSHOT SLI
artifacts carry. Nothing is missing except the unused aaa-authn-api
0.18.4 directory. The scripts are run by hand, e.g.

installation/src/test/docker/image-contract.sh sdnc \
onap/sdnc-image:<tag> 2.3.1-SNAPSHOT

CSIT still fails, for three reasons that are older than this change.
The old image never got far enough in its boot for them to show:
- installCerts.py strips the PEM header from the private key, and
CSIT's generate_certs.sh creates PKCS#8 keys. The Titanium NETCONF
keystore accepts only a complete PKCS#1 PEM ("BEGIN RSA PRIVATE
KEY"). It answers 500 "Invalid private key", and startODL.sh then
stops the container. In OOM this only applies with
global.cmpv2Enabled, the only case in which ODL_CERT_DIR is set.
- ansible-adaptor 2.3.1-SNAPSHOT fails to activate (NoClassDefFoundError
ch/qos/logback/classic/LoggerContext from eelf-core), so it stays
WAITING. SystemReady gives up after its 5-minute diag timeout, and
"warp coils", the line CSIT waits for, appears about 330 s after Karaf
starts, later than CSIT's 300 s limit.
- The mariadb client requires SSL by default, so the CSIT database
dumps are not loaded. The image from master has the same problem.
With the certificate installation skipped, no bundle in this image is
in FAILURE state (466 ACTIVE), and only ansible-adaptor stays WAITING.
I can address the three problems in follow-up changes if that is wanted.

-> sdnc-image

end with FROM scratch + COPY / /, so sdnc-image is a single 1.8 GB
layer and the upstream image underneath can't be seen. A fix in the
JDK, in Alpine or in SLI only reaches SDNC after it has gone through
these releases:

JDK/Alpine fix: alpine-j21 release -> odl-titanium release ->
odlsli release -> version bump + sdnc/oam release
SLI fix: sli release -> odlsli release ->
version bump + sdnc/oam release

runs Alpine 3.21.3, and on master the chain is currently stuck:
- Since merge-verification #212, the base tag 2.3.0-SNAPSHOT-latest is
gone from nexus3 (404), and odlsli cannot publish a new one, because
its pom tags with *.snapshot.version properties that TagVersion.groovy
never sets.
- The rsync step in odlsli and in this Dockerfile fails with the rsync
3.5.0 in current Alpine ("Symbolic link loop", because $ODL_HOME is
the symlink /opt/opendaylight/current).

whatever SLI was newest when odlsli was built, not the
ccsdk.sli.version this repo pins. 3.2.4 pins SLI 2.2.1 but boots
2.2.2-SNAPSHOT. Local odlsli builds of the same master commit gave
2.3.0 one day and 2.3.1-SNAPSHOT the next.

boot features", because ccsdk-sli 2.3.0 pins guava 33.4.0-jre,
commons-lang3 3.17.0 and others that are not in the Titanium system
repository. On master, the sdnc CSIT plan timed out at Karaf start in
#210 and #211. A local build of master shows the boot-feature error.

This change also pins the released a1-adapter 2.3.1 instead of
2.3.0-SNAPSHOT. That snapshot can no longer be resolved, because its
parent odlparent-lite 3.3.3-SNAPSHOT was purged from Nexus after
ccsdk/parent 3.3.3 was released. Since merge-verification #213 every
build of master fails on it while resolving installation/sdnc. The fix
is part of this change because the pin alone would only move master's
build on to the missing odlsli base. 2.3.1 is the released version of
the same code line; its POMs inherit the released ccsdk/parent 3.3.2.

With this change sdnc/oam builds the image itself in an "assemble"
stage. The inputs are Maven artifacts only, no ccsdk/distribution
image:

copies.

old_description:
Run tox on Python 3.11 and drop the dangling basic_intent entry point

setup.cfg requires Python >=3.11, as do the xtesting images that run
these scenarios, but every tox env used python3.10. Use 3.11, the
newest interpreter on the LF Jenkins nodes.

setup.cfg also registered basic_intent =
onaptests.scenario.basic_intent:IntentScenario, but neither that module
nor its settings were ever in this repository: the scenario tests a
non-ONAP intent engine through a non-ONAP SDK and lives in a downstream
fork, which registers the entry point itself. run_test.py validates
every registered entry point, so `tox -e validate` aborted on it with
ModuleNotFoundError on any Python version. Without it validate passes
for all scenarios on 3.11.

The lint jobs run on centos8 nodes, which have no 3.11. They move to
ubuntu2204 nodes in a ci-management change, which has to merge first.

old_description:
[COMMON] Use alpine/psql for postgres client jobs

postgres-init and the uui-server, uui-intent-analysis and
uui-llm-adaptation init jobs only run psql, but pull
crunchy-postgres:centos8-13.2-4.6.1: a PostgreSQL 13.2 server image
on an EOL CentOS 8 base with 1 CRITICAL / 361 HIGH in the gating
Trivy scan. Add a separate psqlImage (alpine/psql:18.6, no CRITICAL
or HIGH findings) and keep postgresImage for the server deployments.

alpine/psql ships no envsubst, so setup.sql now reads its values with
psql's \getenv and :"var" / :'var' interpolation. That also quotes
the password correctly, which made the sed escaping redundant, and
passes the root password via PGPASSWORD instead of the connection
URL. Tested against crunchy-postgres 13.2 with a password containing
quotes, a dollar sign and a space.

The crunchy image ran as uid 26 through its USER, alpine/psql runs as
root, so the uui jobs now get the common pod and container security
contexts.

python-onapsdk's unit tests ran only as py38 and py39, both end-of-life,
on ubuntu1804 nodes, whose newest interpreter is 3.10.6. The package now
requires Python >=3.11, the version the xtesting images run, so py38
and py39 cannot install it any more.

3.11 is on the ubuntu2204 nodes (pyenv 3.11.10 next to 3.8, 3.9 and
3.10). Run tox-verify, the pypi verify/stage/merge jobs and the linters
there, on ubuntu2204-docker-8c-8g, and replace the python3.8 and
python3.9 lint jobs with one python3.11 job. That supersedes the
py310/py311 jobs commented out for IT-25247, an ubuntu1804 limitation.

jenkins-jobs test: 7 jobs change node, py38,py39 becomes py311 and
the python3.8/3.9 lint jobs are replaced; nothing else changes.

The python-onapsdk change requiring 3.11 depends on this one.

Issue-ID: INT-2425

old_description:
Docs: Stop linkcheck failing on warnings

Drop -W from the docs-linkcheck tox environment, so a warning raised
by the linkcheck builder no longer fails the build.

External sites increasingly refuse automated requests, answering a
crawler with 403 or 429 regardless of whether the page exists. With
-W those responses turn into a failed docs job, so a red result
often reflects a third party's bot policy rather than a broken link
in this repository. Genuinely broken links still appear in the
linkcheck output and its report under _build/linkcheck.

The docs environment keeps -W: there it catches real faults in the
documentation source, such as bad references and malformed markup,
which the project controls.

Raised by the RTD audit in the rtdv3 merge workflow, which flagged
the flag as linkcheck-strict on docs/tox.ini line 34.

Issue-ID: CIMAN-33

code changes. Downstream mutating compensation and broader supported-family
scenarios remain follow-up work in this WIP; no slice is declared protected.

old_description:
Chore: Remove the stale INFO.yaml under kubernetes/robot

The file came across with the 2020 reintegration of the robot chart
into this repository (change 116156) and is a copy of the INFO.yaml
of 'testsuite/oom', the project the chart was moved out of. It names
that project, lists its committers and declares its repository, so it
describes neither this repository nor the chart. 'testsuite/oom' is
archived; this repository's governance record is 'INFO.yaml' at the
root, which is valid.

Nothing in the charts, the scripts or CODEOWNERS reads the file.

Found by validating every ONAP INFO.yaml with
lfreleng-actions/info-yaml-validate-action, which the Gerrit
required-verify workflow is moving to.

old_description:
Chore: Remove the stale INFO.yaml and .gitreview under jtosca

Both files came across with the 2019 move of jTosca into this
repository (change 97123) and describe the former project rather
than this one. 'jtosca/.gitreview' names 'sdc/jtosca', which is now
read-only, so git-review run from that directory targets a project
that refuses pushes. 'jtosca/INFO.yaml' lists the 2017 committers of
the former project and has never parsed: its list items are indented
two spaces too deep, and three 'tsc.changes' entries stack several
'name' keys in one mapping. The repository's governance record is
'INFO.yaml' at the root, which is valid.

Nothing in the build or the documentation reads either file.

Found by validating every ONAP INFO.yaml with
lfreleng-actions/info-yaml-validate-action, which the Gerrit
required-verify workflow is moving to.

Policy chart, instead of a dedicated mariadb-galera instance. The
blueprints-processor connects with the PostgreSQL driver and waits for
the PostgreSQL primary service. Set global.postgres.localCluster=false
and global.postgres.service.name2 to use an external PostgreSQL.

The database volume keeps the 3Gi of the old MariaDB, and the Argo
values set its storage class through the postgres subchart.

processor-db keeps pointing at the SDNC MariaDB.

old CDS MariaDB is not migrated automatically. The CDS documentation
describes re-onboarding the CBAs or copying the data with pgloader.

cannot create its tables on PostgreSQL, and images with PostgreSQL
support (ccsdk/cds CCSDK-4219) no longer target MariaDB.

images reads it, so the OTLP exporter was configured whether
global.tracing.enabled was set or not. The opentelemetry-sdk in these
images (1.19.0) does not read OTEL_SDK_DISABLED either, so the
exporter selection is the switch that works.

The switch only has an effect with images whose gRPC servers are
instrumented (CCSDK-4228); the 1.10.0 images create no spans. It
therefore moves with the image update rather than standing alone
(previously OOM-3407).

The 1.11.0 images decrypt endpoints.user.name and endpoints.user.password
with AES/GCM instead of AES/CBC (see the CDS 1.11.0 upgrade notes). The
chart still carried the CBC ciphertext, which no longer decrypts: the
health API then sends empty credentials and every self-check fails with
BadCredentialsException. Both components now use the GCM value the
images ship for ccsdkapps.

The blueprints-processor image ships OpenTelemetry Java agent 2.26.1,
which reads OTEL_CONFIG_FILE and logs a deprecation warning for
OTEL_EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_FILE. sdc-listener keeps the experimental name
for now; its 1.11.0 image ships agent 2.26.1 as well, which still reads
it.

old_description:
Hide Save on the General tab after certify

Certifying a checked-out asset from the General tab left the tab in
edit mode: Save stayed enabled and Contact ID, Description and Tags
stayed editable, so the next Save sent a metadata update for the
certified component and the backend answered 403 "Restricted
operation."

The workspace shell certifies in place rather than reloading the
route, which keeps the shell mounted for Selenium's post-certify page
check, but the General tab only works out its mode in ngOnInit. When
no service depends on the asset, the shell did not recompute its own
mode or the view-only flag in the store either.

The shell now recomputes its mode in the certify case and notifies a
new ON_CERTIFY event, on which the General tab recomputes its mode.
ON_CHECKOUT is not reused: its listeners swap in the component they
are handed. Checked against oom-sm-master through the dev server:
after certify the tab renders like a freshly loaded certified asset.

Issue-ID: SDC-5173
new_description:
Make workspace tabs read-only after certify

Certifying a checked-out asset left the open workspace tab editable.
On the General tab Save stayed enabled and Contact ID, Description
and Tags stayed editable, so the next Save sent a metadata update for
the certified component and the backend answered 403 "Restricted
operation." Properties Assignment, Attributes & Outputs, Operation,
Interface Definition and the VFC Properties tab stayed editable the
same way.

The workspace shell certifies in place rather than reloading the
route, which keeps the shell mounted for Selenium's post-certify page
check, but these tabs only work out whether they are read-only when
they are created, and refresh it only on checkout. When no service
depends on the asset, the shell did not recompute its own mode or the
view-only flag in the store either, so the tabs that read that flag
stayed editable too.

The shell now recomputes its mode in the certify case and notifies a
new ON_CERTIFY event, on which each of these tabs recomputes its
mode. ON_CHECKOUT is not reused: its listeners swap in the component
they are handed. Listeners unregister by reference, because
unRegisterObserver without a callback removes nothing once a second
listener is registered for the event.

Checked against oom-sm-master through the dev server: after certify,
General, Properties Assignment, Attributes & Outputs and Operation
render like a freshly loaded certified asset.

old_description:
Keep the Properties Assignment side panel on screen

Below an 1800px window the right-hand column of Properties Assignment
ran past the window edge and was clipped: at 1600px the Composition /
Property Structure panel and the Add Property button ended at x=1634.

The left column had a fixed min-width of 930px, added for SDC-2328 so
the absolutely positioned search/declare toolbar would not cover the
tabs. With the 350px right column that needs 1294px, while the content
area is 1160px wide at 1600px. 930px was also too little once an
instance is selected: the TOSCA function button makes the toolbar
764px, so tabs and toolbar need about 975px side by side, which the
column only gets from an 1800px window on.

Below 1800px the toolbar now sits above the tabs in normal flow and
may wrap, Discard/Save take the space it leaves next to the tabs, and
the tab strip sizes to its labels. The min-width is gone. The toolbar
comes before the tabs in the markup, so keyboard focus reaches search
and the declare buttons before the table instead of after it. Layout at
1800px and above is unchanged.

The Create List Input button's test id read
"declare-but($event)ton declare-list-input" since 2021; it is now
"declare-button declare-list-input", which the Cypress spec expects.

The new workspace-gutter Playwright test opens the tab on a new VF at
1600px and 1920px and checks that the toolbar does not cover the tabs
and that the right column ends inside the window. It fails without
this change ("run past the viewport at 1600px", 1634 > 1600) and
passes with it, run through the dev server against the oom-sm-master
backend, together with the other three tests in the file. Measured
there as well at 1280-1920px, with and without an instance selected:
no overlap and no horizontal scroll. Jest for the page and
npm run build:prod pass.

Below an 1800px window the right-hand column of Properties Assignment
ran past the window edge and was clipped: at 1600px the Composition /
Property Structure panel and the Add Property button ended at x=1634.

The left column had a fixed min-width of 930px, added for SDC-2328 so
the absolutely positioned search/declare toolbar would not cover the
tabs. With the 350px right column that needs 1294px, while the content
area is 1160px wide at 1600px. 930px was also too little once an
instance is selected: the TOSCA function button makes the toolbar

column only gets from an 1800px window on.

Below 1800px the toolbar now sits above the tabs in normal flow and
may wrap, Discard/Save take the space it leaves next to the tabs, and

comes before the tabs in the markup, so keyboard focus reaches search
and the declare buttons before the table instead of after it. Layout at
1800px and above is unchanged; there the toolbar stays absolutely
positioned over the tab row and now carries z-index: 1, because the
positioned .main-tabs-section comes after it and its full-width <tabs>
host would otherwise take every click on search and the declare buttons
(UI CSIT on PS1: declareInputFromProperties, ElementClickIntercepted).

The Create List Input button's test id read
"declare-but($event)ton declare-list-input" since 2021; it is now
"declare-button declare-list-input", which the Cypress spec expects.

The new workspace-gutter Playwright test opens the tab on a new VF at
1600px and 1920px and checks that the toolbar does not cover the tabs,
that every enabled toolbar control receives a click at its centre, and
that the right column ends inside the window. It fails on master ("run
past the viewport at 1600px", 1634 > 1600) and without the z-index
("hidden under another element at 1920px"), and passes with this
change, run through the dev server against the oom-sm-master
backend, together with the other tests in the file. Declare Input and TOSCA
function also pass Playwright's click actionability check at both widths
with a row checked. Measured
there as well at 1280-1920px, with and without an instance selected:
no overlap and no horizontal scroll. Jest for the page and
npm run build:prod pass.

Updates `org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable` from 0.2.11 to 0.2.12
## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

Updates `org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` from 3.1.0 to 3.1.1
## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

New Contributors

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

Updates `org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable` from 0.2.11 to 0.2.12
## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

Updates `org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` from 3.1.0 to 3.1.1
## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

New Contributors
