## Release notes

Sourced from org.springdoc:springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui's releases.

springdoc-openapi v3.1.1 released!
Security

GHSA-6f5m-mhjg-qwxq – MCP tool callbacks do not encode path parameters, allowing request retargeting
GHSA-4v2q-56v7-2cpw – MCP transport, admin and dashboard endpoints are exposed by default
GHSA-m4cg-mhpg-rh2r – MCP audit events record credentials and request/response bodies without redaction
GHSA-5f9r-4mc4-qh3c – Unbounded MCP pending-confirmation store allows memory exhaustion
GHSA-jcgg-59c8-w4wh – MCP request context in a ThreadLocal can leak headers between concurrent WebFlux requests
GHSA-rhhx-6j8h-8cvw – Unbounded per-locale OpenAPI cache allows memory exhaustion via Accept-Language
GHSA-c925-vm88-mpp9 – Scalar starters trust client-supplied forwarded headers and render from a shared mutable bean
CVE-2026-75838 – Cross-site scripting in the DOMPurify bundled with swagger-ui, addressed by upgrading swagger-ui to 5.32.14

Added

#3340 – Describe JsonNullable values without their Java wrapper
#3325 – Manage the swagger artifacts in springdoc-openapi-bom, so that modules holding only the annotations stay in lockstep
#3321 – Add springdoc.login-endpoint.username-example and springdoc.login-endpoint.password-example to document the Spring Security login endpoint

Changed

MCP is now opt-in. Set springdoc.ai.mcp.enabled=true, and springdoc.ai.mcp.dashboard-enabled=true for the dashboard
The Scalar starters no longer register forwarded-header handling. Set server.forward-headers-strategy=framework (or native) behind a trusted proxy
Add springdoc.cache.max-entries (default 100) to bound the per-locale OpenAPI cache
Add springdoc.ai.mcp.audit.redact (default true) to mask secrets in MCP audit events
Document that the MCP approval flow is a confirmation step, not an authorization control
Document the security policy and the release versioning scheme
#3351 – java.time.Duration, LocalTime and OffsetTime are now resolved by swagger-core instead of being forced to a bare string, so they carry a format (duration and partial-time respectively for the first two)
A property whose type only implements Set indirectly (LinkedHashSet, TreeSet, …) is now described with uniqueItems: true, following swagger-api/swagger-core#5265
Upgrade swagger-core to version 2.2.55
Upgrade swagger-ui to version 5.32.14

Fixed

#3328, #3337 – /v3/api-docs fails with a NullPointerException when spring-hateoas is on the classpath without HateoasProperties
#3314 – Json Processing Exception occurred is logged for every constrained parameter whose schema is not a JsonSchema
#3317 – An injected HttpHeaders parameter is described as a schema
#3332 – The properties a Kotlin entity inherits from an @Embeddable are missing from the Spring Data REST schemas
#3320 – @Order and Ordered ignored when applying customizers
#3319 – A Page nested in another schema is not replaced by PagedModel
#3313 – Springdoc auto-configurations rely on unspecified auto-configuration ordering
#3331 – Validation annotations declared inside Optional parameters are dropped
#3322 – Validation annotations on a container's type argument leak between parameters
#3315 – An OAS 3.1 JsonSchema cannot be cloned through JSON
#3300 – TYPE_USE annotations on @ParameterObject fields are not passed along
#3341 – Stabilize Spring Data Sort and Pageable schema property order
#3338 – Kotlin nullability interpretation of the Any? type
#3136 – A Spring Data REST association to a non-exported entity expands its @EmbeddedId and @MapsId fields recursively in the response schemas
The Spring Data REST response post-processing rewrote an association property in place, so the …Response refs could leak into the schema shared with the request body representation

## Release notes

Sourced from org.openapitools:jackson-databind-nullable's releases.

v0.2.12 released
Highlights

New mapBlankStringToNull option on both modules: with it on, a blank string for a non-String JsonNullable reads as of(null) instead of undefined() (#186, thanks @​Thorsrud22, and @​krangerich for the first version in #126).
Character, CharSequence and deserializers you register yourself now get the empty string instead of undefined() (#187, fixes #26 and #46). Two cases behave differently from 0.2.11: a wrapper deserializer that neither extends DelegatingDeserializer nor overrides getDelegatee() is judged by its own class, so the deserializer it wraps can now throw on ""; and a subclass of FromStringDeserializer now reads "" as of(null). Content converters (@JsonDeserialize(contentConverter = ...)) still don't see "". Thanks @​Thorsrud22 for testing it past the suite.

Docs: module-path registration on Java 17+ (#188) and what NON_NULL does in the usage example (#190).
CI runs on JDK 17, 21 and 25 (#171), and CreatorTest is back on (#170), thanks @​davidpavlovschi.

Base the processor and sdclistener images on eclipse-temurin

The blueprintsprocessor image was built on
onap/ccsdk-alpine-j21-image:2.2.1 (Java 21.0.6, Alpine 3.21) and the
sdclistener image on onap/ccsdk-alpine-j17-image:1.5.1 (built in March
2023, Java 17.0.6, Alpine 3.17). Both are eclipse-temurin JRE Alpine
plus sudo, bash, git, nodejs, npm, python3, py3-pip, mysql-client,
graphviz, rsync, unzip, iputils, openssl and nss. Those packages carry
most of the vulnerabilities of the images, and nothing in CDS uses
them: the start scripts only run java, neither service starts external
processes (Python scripts run in Jython, Kotlin scripts are compiled
in the JVM), and the probes are HTTP probes.

Build both images directly on eclipse-temurin:21-jre-alpine and create
the onap user with uid/gid 1000, which the OOM fix-permission init
container already chowns the blueprint volume to. sdclistener now runs
on Java 21 as well. The floating tag keeps the images on the latest
Java 21 and Alpine patch level without a bump for every update.

Trivy, OS packages, against the 1.10.0 images:
- blueprintsprocessor: 3 critical / 24 high -> 0 / 1
- sdclistener: 5 critical / 45 high -> 0 / 1
The blueprintsprocessor image shrinks from 1.42 GB to 1.07 GB.

Verified locally: the blueprintsprocessor image starts against
PostgreSQL, publishes the capability_cli test CBA and executes its
Kotlin script (compiled at runtime) successfully; sdclistener starts
and stops at the Kafka SASL configuration, like the 1.11.0 staging
image does without it.

old_description:
Fix: Make testSetConfiguration_InvalidDir host independent

The test points configurationPath at /opt/path and expects
setConfigurationDir() to raise. That method only raises when
Files.createDirectories() fails, so the assertion depends on whether
the build account can write /opt rather than on the behaviour of the
code under test.

That assumption holds on the Jenkins build node and does not hold on a
GitHub-hosted runner, where the job runs as a user that can create
/opt/path: the directory is created, nothing is raised, and the test
fails. The same revision passes on Jenkins and fails on GitHub Actions
for that reason alone.

Point the path below an existing regular file instead. Creating a
directory under a file fails with ENOTDIR, which is a filesystem rule
rather than a permission, so it holds for every user on every host,
root included. A permission-based alternative such as chmod would
still pass or fail depending on who runs the build.

echo.drl already serves as the not-a-directory fixture for
testSetConfiguration_FileIsNotDirectory in this class, so no new test
resource is needed.

Issue-ID: CIMAN-33
new_description:
Fix: Make testSetConfiguration_InvalidDir host independent

The test points configurationPath at /opt/path and expects
setConfigurationDir() to raise. That method only raises when
Files.createDirectories() fails, so the assertion depends on whether
the build account can write /opt rather than on the behaviour of the
code under test.

That assumption holds on the Jenkins build node and does not hold on a
GitHub-hosted runner, where the job runs as a user that can create
/opt/path: the directory is created, nothing is raised, and the test
fails. The same revision passes on Jenkins and fails on GitHub Actions
for that reason alone.

Build the unwritable directory in the test instead of borrowing one
from the host. A temporary directory with its write bit cleared gives
the same conditions on any machine: the target does not exist, so
Files.notExists() is true and the create branch is entered, and the
create then fails with EACCES, which is the IOException the method
turns into "cannot create".

The reachability of that branch is a permission question, so there is
no filesystem-level substitute. Pointing below a regular file, for
instance, fails the stat with ENOTDIR rather than ENOENT, which leaves
Files.notExists() false; the method then skips the create entirely and
reports "is not a directory" from the following branch, testing
something the class already covers elsewhere.

A user that bypasses directory permissions cannot reach the branch at
all, so the test assumes its way out rather than failing there.

old_description:
Run UI sanity test classes in parallel

The ui verify job takes about 45 minutes, and about 23 of them are
onapUiSanity.xml running its 33 tests one after another. The suite now
runs its classes on 4 threads, longest class first. On a local stack
that takes the suite from 24m20s to about 11 minutes. The CI node and
the Firefox grid (SE_NODE_MAX_SESSIONS=8) already have room for it.

Parallel load exposed timing bugs in the tests:

- All browsers saved into one download directory, which is wiped
after every test. Each test thread now gets its own sub-directory.
- The CSAR and TOSCA template download flows took the newest file in
the directory after a 0 s wait, so a test that downloads more than
once could read the previous file. They now wait for a new,
completed download.
- The composition sidebar was read right after clicking a canvas node.
It is now polled until it shows the selected node.
- The vendor, model, category and ETSI version dropdowns were read
before their options had loaded from the backend. They now wait for
the option.

The download fix showed that EtsiOnboardVnfCnfUiTests never checked
the service CSAR: it read the resource CSAR a second time. In a
service CSAR the onboarded package sits under
Artifacts/<resource node type>_v1.0/Deployment/ETSI_PACKAGE, so the
service check now expects that path.

(1000:101 for blueprints-processor and sdc-listener, 1000:1000 for
the others); the pods that share the blueprints volume use fsGroup
1000, so they do not change its group on each mount
- fix-permission keeps running as root, but only with CHOWN and
DAC_READ_SEARCH; with CHOWN alone chown -R fails on directories the
application created with mode 700
- cds-ui gets a read-only root filesystem and a /tmp emptyDir, since it
buffers uploaded CBAs there; the executors run CBA code (venvs, pip,
tempfile) and the JVM components were not verified read-only, so
they keep a writable root filesystem
- add a startupProbe to command-executor, py-executor and cds-ui and
drop initialDelaySeconds from all probes; no startup budget gets
shorter (blueprints-processor 310s, the others 120s, before 60-80s
until the first liveness failure)
- cds-ui probes the HTTP paths its values already declared (/ and
/ping) instead of the TCP port; py-executor's readiness probe reads
readiness.port
- cds-ui reads the blueprints-processor auth tokens from a Secret
instead of literal env values; the values stay where they were
- set sizeLimit on the emptyDir volumes, and add checksum/config to
blueprints-processor and sdc-listener so a ConfigMap change rolls
their pods
- command-executor gets a flavor key, which it lacked, so a standalone
deployment rendered no resources, and uses
common.readinessCheck.waitFor instead of a hand-written init
container; the blueprints-processor init containers get resources
- the blueprints-processor Services, PV and PVC use the common labels;
their names and selectors are unchanged, and the ServiceMonitor uses
the default selector, which matches the same Service
- remove values no template reads: the top-level application values of
the umbrella chart, debugEnabled, subChartsOnly, command-executor's
config.basicAuth, the sdc-listener name and the ingress blocks of the
components without an ingress template

Not changed: the blueprints-processor probes keep the literal
Authorization header, since every processor path requires
authentication and probe headers cannot come from a Secret; the SDNC
and AAI credentials in application.properties; the disabled
blueprints-processor liveness probe; the cds-ui NodePort.

Verified with helm template against the parent change: in the default,
large and unlimited flavor, tracing and metrics, ingress,
nodeSelector/affinity and command-executor persistence renders, only the changes above
differ, and every ServiceMonitor still selects the same Service. helm
lint passes for every component. With docker, using the image users,
all capabilities dropped and no-new-privileges: command-executor,
py-executor and cds-ui start and listen as before, and cds-ui accepts
a CBA upload with a read-only root and /tmp mounted, where it fails
without /tmp; blueprints-processor and sdc-listener stop at the same
point with and without these settings (missing database and
configuration), so they were not run to a steady state. The envsubst
init container works unchanged as uid 1000 with a read-only root.

Issue-ID: OOM-3412

old_description:
Cache the category hierarchy in the backend

GET /sdc2/rest/v1/setup/ui gates the catalog UI bootstrap. On a live
deployment Jaeger showed a median of 640 ms server-side with 122 DB
spans, 104 of them serial SELECTs on sdctitan.edgestore. About 87 % of
that is ElementOperation.getAllCategories walking categories, then
sub-categories, then groupings one vertex at a time (20 categories and
49 sub-categories on the test deployment). The result is the same for
every user and only changes on category writes, and the servlet ETag is
computed after the response is built, so it saves no server work.

ElementOperation now keeps the hierarchy per category node type in a
CategoryHierarchyCache. Caching at the operation layer covers every
reader (setup/ui, the category servlet, resource/service import
validation, product validation, the external CRUD API) and keeps the
cache next to every write that touches category, sub-category and
grouping vertices: create/update/delete category, create/update/delete
sub-category, create/delete grouping. That includes the categories
import run by sdc-be-init, which goes through the same methods.

- Every write invalidates after its own commit/rollback, and a load
only stores its result if no invalidation happened while it ran, so
a read racing a write cannot re-cache the old hierarchy.
- Reads with inTransaction=true are served from the cache but never
stored, because they may see the caller's uncommitted writes.
- Callers get deep copies: CrudExternalServlet trims the sub-category
list of the returned category in place.
- Failed reads are not cached.

Another sdc-be replica's write does not reach this pod's cache, so
entries also expire after categoriesCacheTtlInSeconds (default 60 when
the key is absent, 0 disables the cache). OOM runs a single replica by
default, which makes the expiry a safety net rather than the normal
invalidation path.

new_description:
Mark up page headings and landmarks

Screen reader users could not jump by heading or region: no page in
catalog-ui or the onboarding UI had an <h1>, most had no heading at
all, the top navigation was not a banner and sat inside <main> on the
workspace, and the workspace and onboarding side menus were plain
divs. axe did not flag it because 4.12's page-has-heading-one passes
on a page without an <h1>.

Each page now has one <h1>: the asset, VLM or VSP name above its side
menu, "Available Versions - <name>" on the versions page, a visually
hidden "Dashboard", "Catalog" or admin tab name, and a visually hidden
asset name on the composition canvas. Tab titles, the composition
panel title, the onboarding page and section titles (GridSection,
landing page, vendor page) are <h2>; the admin category headers move
from <h4> to <h2> so no level is skipped. The top navigation is a
<header> holding <nav aria-label="Main"> with a search region, it no
longer sits inside the workspace <main>, the side menus are <nav>
landmarks, and the plugin page gets the <main> its skip link targets.

The look is unchanged: the new heading resets (.sdc-heading-reset() in
heading-reset.less, @mixin heading-reset in _utils.scss, now imported
ahead of _layout.scss) strip the UA and Bootstrap heading margins,
size, weight and line height before each class's own rules. All 28
pixel-probe pages compare identical to master, and every converted
heading measures the same as a div twin swapped in its place.

The axe ratchet (expectAxeRatchet) now also requires exactly one
rendered <h1>. Selenium locators that pinned the old tag now ask for
h1 (navbar-group-name) or h2 (tab titles, selectedCompTitle).

Also fixes two locators left behind by the button conversion: the
outputs delete icon is a <button>, and an operation's name in the
composition Interface Operations tab sits in a button inside
span.field-name, so DELETE_OUTPUT_BTN and FIELD_NAME_SPAN failed
addOutputsToVF_test, updateInterfaceOperation and both ImportVfcUiTest
addVFC2VF flows in onapUiSanity.

old_description:
feat: use longest match to resolve cm handle references on NCMP

- Legacy NCMP interfaces used an exact match on the alternate id, unlike
the ProvMnS interface and the data job examiners which already use
longest matching
- A descendant FDN now resolves to the cm handle registered at its
nearest ancestor, so callers need not know the exact registration point
- Read and write operations both resolve this way, so a write to an
unregistered descendant now routes to its ancestor instead of failing
- Call sites reuse the existing getCmHandleIdByLongestMatchingAlternateId
rather than adding a second resolution method with its own exception
- Each legacy interface handles NoAlternateIdMatchFoundException as its
own contract requires: the controller falls back to the raw reference so
a plain cm handle id still reaches the service layer, bulk data
operations skip unresolved references, and the inventory facade
translates it to CmHandleNotFoundException to preserve the 404 mapping
and the empty-list behaviour of the module methods

old_description:
Make CDS JPA mappings work on PostgreSQL

The LONGTEXT/LONGBLOB column definitions only exist on MySQL and
MariaDB, so on PostgreSQL the schema DDL fails and the tables are never
created; @Lob byte arrays would additionally be stored as large
objects. Map the large text columns to TEXT and the CBA archive to
BYTEA and drop @Lob, so values are bound as plain strings and bytes.

Portable Hibernate alternatives were tried and rejected:
SqlTypes.LONG32VARCHAR and Length.LONG32 both stop the tags columns
from being treated as strings, which breaks the existing
findByTagsContainingIgnoreCase queries (upper() argument check), the
latter on the H2 version used by the unit tests.

Existing MariaDB schemas are not altered by hibernate ddl-auto=update,
but a fresh MariaDB is no longer supported: the new DDL uses BYTEA.

Add the PostgreSQL JDBC driver and a Testcontainers test that runs
the JPA context against PostgreSQL 13, the version deployed by OOM:
column types, a 5 MiB CBA round trip with multi-byte text, and a
native resource resolution query. The test is skipped when no Docker
daemon is available.

Issue-ID: CCSDK-4219
new_description:
Make CDS JPA mappings work on PostgreSQL

The LONGTEXT/LONGBLOB column definitions only exist on MySQL and
MariaDB, so on PostgreSQL the schema DDL fails and the tables are never
created; @Lob byte arrays would additionally be stored as large
objects. Drop @Lob and the vendor column definitions and declare the
large text columns and the CBA archive with length = Length.LONG32, so
values are bound as plain strings and bytes and each dialect picks its
own unbounded type: text/bytea on PostgreSQL, longtext/longblob on
MariaDB, clob/blob on H2.

The tags columns are the exception and use columnDefinition = "TEXT":
with Length.LONG32 (or SqlTypes.LONG32VARCHAR) Hibernate no longer
treats them as strings on H2, and the findByTagsContainingIgnoreCase
queries fail their upper() argument check. TEXT exists on all three
databases; on MariaDB it caps tags at 64 KiB.

MariaDB stays fully supported, since it is still the default database
and is what the end-to-end ITs run against. Existing schemas are not
altered by hibernate ddl-auto=update.

Add the PostgreSQL JDBC driver and a Testcontainers test that runs
the JPA context against PostgreSQL 13, the version deployed by OOM:
column types, a 5 MiB CBA round trip with multi-byte text, and a
native resource resolution query. The test is skipped when no Docker
daemon is available.

old_description:
Instrument gRPC servers of command-executor and py-executor

Both services run under opentelemetry-instrument, but
opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc was never installed, so their gRPC
servers were not instrumented, the traceparent sent by
blueprintsprocessor was ignored and every trace ended at the hop to
the Python services.

Installing the instrumentation is not enough on its own:

- opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc 0.40b0, the release matching
opentelemetry-distro 0.40b0, declares grpcio ~= 1.27 but imports
grpc.aio.ClientCallDetails, which grpcio only exposes from 1.33.
With the pinned 1.20.0 and 1.25.0 the instrumentor is skipped as a
dependency conflict, and with 1.27.2 or 1.32.0 its import fails and
opentelemetry-instrument aborts the whole auto-initialisation.
grpcio and grpcio-tools are therefore bumped to 1.33.2, the oldest
release that works. artifact-manager is bumped as well, because its
requirements are installed into the py-executor image and tox env
and would otherwise conflict.
- The instrumentor inserts its interceptor into the interceptors
argument of grpc.server(), which fails at startup with the tuple
both servers passed. They now pass a list.

Verified on python:3.7-slim: with the real command-executor and
py-executor servers started under opentelemetry-instrument, a call
carrying a traceparent produces a SERVER span with that trace id and
the caller's span as parent. The command-executor, py-executor and
artifact-manager unit tests pass.

servers were not instrumented, the traceparent sent by

- opentelemetry-instrumentation-grpc 0.40b0, the release matching

the caller's span as parent. The command-executor, py-executor and
artifact-manager unit tests pass on Python 3.7, and the py-executor

old_description:
Read Zusammen subtrees in one call

listElementData did a list plus one get per child, and getServiceModel
listed the service model twice and read every template and artifact
row twice, sequentially. Both now use the Zusammen element subtree
read (ElementAdaptor.getTree), which reads each level's rows
concurrently.

This depends on the Zusammen release that carries getTree, 1.2.0, not
1.1.0, and must go in on top of the change pinning onboarding to it.

Child order is unchanged: both the old list and the tree read walk
the same parent's sub_element_ids.

For a non-null parent, a missing item version now yields an empty
list rather than an error, because the tree read does not go through
ElementManagerImpl.list's version-existence check; all current
callers resolve the parent through a validated path first.

Issue-ID: SDC-4993
new_description:
Read Zusammen subtrees in one call

Zusammen 1.2.0 adds an element subtree read (ElementAdaptor.getTree)
that reads each level's rows concurrently. Pin onboarding to it and use
it where SDC fetched a parent and then each child with its own
sequential get:

- listElementData did a list plus one get per child
- getServiceModel listed the service model twice and read every
template and artifact row twice
- the orchestration template read and the candidate get and getInfo
read the parent and then each of its children separately

Child order is unchanged: both the old list and the tree read walk
the same parent's sub_element_ids.

For a non-null parent, a missing item version now yields an empty
list rather than an error, because the tree read does not go through
ElementManagerImpl.list's version-existence check; all current
callers resolve the parent through a validated path first.

The candidate getInfo now also reads the candidate row itself, which
holds only the files data structure; its children were already read
in full.

old_description:
Bump vulnerable libraries within their release lines

Raise the root-pom versions behind the HIGH Trivy findings in the
frontend image to the lowest release that fixes every reported
finding, staying on Java 11 and within what Spring Boot 2.7 runs on:

- jackson 2.14.2 -> 2.18.11
- snakeyaml 1.33 -> 2.3 (the version jackson-dataformat-yaml 2.18 uses)
- logback 1.2.12 -> 1.2.13
- spring 5.3.27 -> 5.3.39
- httpclient5 5.2.1 -> 5.6.3 (httpcore5 5.2 -> 5.4.3)
- commons-io 2.13.0 -> 2.14.0
- commons-lang3 3.12.0 -> 3.18.0
- jsoup 1.15.3 -> 1.23.2
- commons-beanutils 1.9.4 -> 1.11.0
- OpenTelemetry agent and annotations 2.26.1 -> 2.28.0

logback stays on 1.2, because 1.3 needs slf4j 2, which Spring Boot 2.7
cannot use.

jackson-annotations and commons-beanutils are now managed, because
security-util-lib and commons-validator brought in 2.15.2 and 1.9.4.
jackson-module-jaxb-annotations 2.18 switched from
jakarta.xml.bind-api 2.3.3 to javax.xml.bind:jaxb-api 2.2.12, which has
no javax.activation dependency. Both JAXB APIs are managed at today's
versions so that JAXB does not move. The jackson-bom is not imported
because its parent manages jaxb-api at 2.2.12 as well.

Across the -P all reactor, mvn dependency:list changes only these
libraries plus woodstox 7.0.0 / stax2 4.2.2 (jackson-dataformat-xml),
commons-logging 1.3.5 (beanutils) and opentelemetry-api 1.62.0.

snakeyaml 2 removed the no-argument Constructor and Representer
constructors. The call sites now pass new LoaderOptions() or
new DumperOptions(), which is what snakeyaml 1.33 used internally, so
loading and dumping behave the same: all 1247 service templates
under src/test/resources load and dump to byte-identical YAML with
both versions.

old_description:
Add Kafka topic readiness check using SmartLifecycle

Ensure Kafka listener containers in both runtime-acm and
participant-intermediary only start after required topics are
available on the broker. Each module provides a SmartLifecycle
component that waits for topics, starts listeners, and runs
module-specific initialization (e.g. participant registration,
status request broadcast) before accepting messages.

- Add AbstractKafkaLifecycle in common module with topic wait loop,
configurable timeout, and start/stop hooks for subclasses
- Use KafkaAdmin.describeTopics for readiness check, which implicitly
verifies broker connectivity (replaces raw AdminClient health check)
- Add KafkaLifecycle in runtime-acm (send status request on start)
- Add KafkaLifecycle in participant-intermediary (register participant
and startsheartbeat scheduler on start; deregister on stop)
- Remove KafkaStartup, KafkaHealthCheck, KafkaReadinessHealthIndicator
and ParticipantLifecycleHandler (replaced by lifecycle components)
- Rename MessageSender to HeartbeatSender and move scheduling from
ContextRefreshedEvent to explicit startScheduler() called by
KafkaLifecycle
- Remove topicValidation and kafkaHealthCheck config parameters
(topic check is now always-on and built into the lifecycle)
- Simplify compose health checks and CSIT registration test

old_description:
Make SVGIcon, Accordion, Tabs, Modal and Tile accessible

Several components could only be used with a mouse and exposed no
roles or states to screen readers. A shared keyboardClick helper
activates on Enter and Space, but only for keys pressed on the
element itself, so a nested control never fires its host twice.

- SVGIcon: with onClick it is a role=button with a tab stop and an
ariaLabel prop; disabled now also blocks the mouse click. Icons
without onClick or label are aria-hidden.
- Accordion: the header is a button with aria-expanded and
aria-controls pointing at the body.
- Tabs: aria-selected, a roving tabindex, tab/panel id linkage,
arrow/Home/End navigation and aria-disabled.
- Modal: role=dialog with aria-modal, labelled by its title; focus
moves into the dialog on open and returns to the opener on close,
and Escape calls an optional onClose. The close icon is named by a
closeAriaLabel prop (default 'Close').
- Notification: role=alert for errors and warnings, status otherwise.
- Tile: with onClick it is a keyboard operable button.
- Input and RadioGroup: aria-invalid/aria-describedby/aria-required
on the input, radiogroup labelled by its title.

Move to onap-ui-common 1.2.0, which carries the focus-ring and
contrast styles these roles rely on, and regenerate iconMap.js for
its new icons. 1.2.0 is published only to ONAP Nexus, so a project
.npmrc points npm at npm.public.

Issue-ID: SDC-5071
new_description:
Use native elements for SVGIcon, Accordion, Tabs, Modal and Tile

Several components could only be used with a mouse and exposed no
roles or states to screen readers. Native elements give keyboard
activation, focusability, disabled handling and (for <dialog>) the
focus trap, inertness and Escape for free, so they replace the ARIA
roles and key handlers a div would need.

Markup changes consumers can see:
- SVGIcon with onClick renders <button type="button"> (same classes)
with an ariaLabel prop; a native disabled button gets no click.
Icons without onClick stay a div, aria-hidden when unlabelled.
- Accordion: the header is <button class="sdc-accordion-header">
with aria-expanded/aria-controls; the chevron wrapper and the title
are spans, not divs. A new disabled prop disables the header button.
- Tabs: <li class="sdc-tab" role="presentation"> keeps its classes
and data-test-id and wraps <button class="sdc-tab__button"
role="tab">, with aria-selected, a roving tabindex, tab/panel id
linkage and arrow/Home/End navigation. The button owns the li's
padding and the click handler, and disabled moves onto it.
- Modal: while show is true the .sdc-modal element is a <dialog>
opened with showModal(), labelled by its title when there is one;
when show turns false or the Modal unmounts it is closed, which
returns focus, and removed. A hidden Modal renders no dialog.
Escape calls an optional onClose; the dialog stays open until show
turns false. modal={false} opens it with show() instead, outside
the top layer, for consumers whose body-level overlays (tooltips,
notifications) must stay usable while it is open. With onClose
the close icon is <button class="svg-icon-wrapper
sdc-modal__close-button-svg sdc-modal__close-button bottom"> named
by closeAriaLabel (default 'Close').
- RadioGroup: <fieldset> with a <legend> title.
- Tile: the card is a plain div; with onClick the header text is
<button class="sdc-tile-header-button"> whose ::after covers the
card. It is named by headerText or by a new ariaLabel prop (one of
the two is required with onClick). Clicks on the card's own footer
buttons no longer also fire the tile's onClick.
- Notification: role=alert for errors and warnings, status otherwise.
- Input: aria-invalid/aria-describedby/aria-required.

onap-ui-common 1.2.0 still styles these as divs. Until 1.3.0 ships
sdc-button-reset, src/style/_native-elements.scss mirrors its button
reset (same selectors), focus rings and tab padding, and adds the
Tile stretched-link rule, a fieldset reset and the <dialog> UA-style
overrides, which have no onap-ui-common counterpart.

Move to onap-ui-common 1.2.0, which carries the focus-ring and
contrast styles, and regenerate iconMap.js for its new icons. 1.2.0
is published only to ONAP Nexus, so a project .npmrc points npm at
npm.public.

old_description:
Use native buttons for icon, accordion, tab and modal close

The clickable icon, the accordion header, the tab and the modal close
button were divs and lis given role, tabindex and key handling by the
framework libraries. A native button provides focus, Enter/Space
activation and disabled for free, so onap-ui-angular and onap-ui-react
no longer need key-handling JS for them.

The reference HTML now uses button type="button" for these four, and a
new sdc-button-reset mixin strips the user-agent button styling so they
render as before. The focus rings cover the new button selectors.

For consumers:
- svg-icon-wrapper (when clickable), sdc-accordion-header and the modal
close button change from div to button. The accordion title and
chevron wrapper change from div to span, because a div is not valid
inside a button.
- The tab role moves from the li to an inner button.sdc-tab__button;
the li keeps the visual classes and gets role="presentation", and
disabled moves to the button.
- Selectors that pin the div or li markup must be updated.

Issue-ID: SDC-5076
new_description:
Use native elements for icon, accordion, tab, modal, tile and radios

The clickable icon, the accordion header, the tab and the modal close
button were divs and lis given role, tabindex and key handling by the
framework libraries. A native button provides focus, Enter/Space
activation and disabled for free, so onap-ui-angular and onap-ui-react
no longer need key-handling JS for them. Likewise a native dialog gives
the modal Escape, inertness and a focus trap, and a fieldset with a
legend names a radio group.

The reference HTML now uses button type="button" for these four, and a
new sdc-button-reset mixin strips the user-agent button styling so they
render as before. The focus rings cover the new button selectors. New
references and styles cover a dialog modal, a tile whose header is a
button stretched over the card, and a fieldset radio group, which
onap-ui-react renders.

For consumers:
- svg-icon-wrapper (when clickable), sdc-accordion-header and the modal
close button change from div to button. The accordion title and
chevron wrapper change from div to span, because a div is not valid
inside a button.
- A clickable icon without a label is a bare button.svg-icon-wrapper;
mode-*, size-* and clickable sit on the inner .svg-icon, because the
wrapper's mode rules give different hover colours.
- The tab role moves from the li to an inner button.sdc-tab__button;
the li keeps the visual classes and gets role="presentation", and
disabled moves to the button.
- The modal may be a dialog.sdc-modal opened with showModal(); a closed
dialog is hidden. The div modal is still supported.
- A clickable tile carries button.sdc-tile-header-button inside
.sdc-tile-header, and the card itself is no longer the control.
- A radio group may be fieldset.sdc-radio-group with
legend.sdc-radio-group__legend.
- Selectors that pin the div or li markup must be updated.

old_description:
Add end-to-end ITs for REST resolution and persistence

The blueprints processor has no test that follows a request out of the
JVM: the UAT suite swaps the southbound REST client for an in-process
mock and stores everything in H2.

Add failsafe ITs in the application module that boot the full processor
against real infrastructure, started once per JVM and shared by one
Spring context: MariaDB 11.7.2 (the version OOM deploys) via
Testcontainers as both the primary database and the processor-db
resource source, and WireMock as the REST resource source. A small
purpose-built CBA (e2e-it) resolves a hostname from the input, a
vlan-id over HTTP and a management IP from the processor DB, and
stores the result.

- RestSouthboundIT: the vlan-id is fetched over HTTP with basic auth;
an inventory error fails the workflow because the value is required.
- PersistenceIT: publishing stores BLUEPRINT_MODEL and its archive;
resource assignment stores RESOURCE_RESOLUTION and
TEMPLATE_RESOLUTION rows, which the resources API returns.

Unbind the failsafe execution inherited from the Spring Boot parent.
It ran every IT a second time, without the JaCoCo agent that the
integration-tests execution attaches.

old_description:
Document blueprintsprocessor runtime limit properties

blueprintsprocessor.grpcMaxInboundMessageSize and the
jackson.stream-read-constraints.* properties were added recently, but
they appear only as commented-out lines in application.properties.
Operators who hit a RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED gRPC error or a Jackson
"String length exceeds the maximum" error have to read the Kotlin
sources to find out what they can tune and what the defaults are.

Add a configuration page that describes these properties together with
the related gRPC server switches, their defaults (the Jackson defaults
taken from the bundled jackson-core 2.20), and how to set them as
environment variables. Link it from the installation guide, next to
the note about customizing application.properties in OOM.

old_description:
Fix the generated blueprintsprocessor swagger spec

The committed cds-bp-processor-api-swagger.json is not valid JSON, so
the docs had to stop rendering it and every client that parses it
fails. With jsonExampleValues=true the swagger-maven-plugin writes the
example of non-string properties as a raw JSON token, and the
"2012-04-23T18:25:43.511Z" example of the Date timestamps ends up
unquoted. Drop the option: the remaining examples come out the same.

Three operations were missing from the spec: POST /api/v1/model-type
and GET/DELETE /api/v1/template. The plugin drops a method mapping
with path [""]; Spring maps it the same as a mapping without a path,
so remove the empty path. ModelTypeControllerWebTest covers the
POST route over HTTP, TemplateControllerTest already covers the other
two.

Substitute JsonNode and ObjectNode with Object. The spec described
them through Jackson's getters (nodeType, pojo, ...), which is not
what the API sends, and the order of those properties changed on
every build.

Also drop a trailing space from two operation summaries, which broke
the RST that sphinxcontrib-openapi generates, and render the spec in
the API reference again.

The health-check endpoints are not added: they are annotated with
hidden = true. Message prioritization and workflow audit status live
in modules the blueprintsprocessor application does not include, and
the UAT endpoints exist only with the uat profile.

The property order of some models, such as the Spring Data Page,
still follows reflection order and can change between builds; the
plugin has no option to sort model properties.
